papers.title: IL-4 and arginine synergy accelerates early bone regeneration via enhanced efferocytosis and ameliorated microenvironment.
papers.abstract: Host bone microenvironment is a critical factor for successful bone regeneration during implantation. In this work, we identified a spatiotemporal mismatch at drilling-induced injury sites where initial apoptosis outpaces macrophage recruitment, leading to apoptotic cell accumulation and oxidative stress that impairs osteogenic differentiation. To mitigate this phenomenon, we developed a synergistic strategy co-delivering interleukin 4 (IL-4) and arginine (Arg) to reprogram the microenvironment. Mechanistically, IL-4 recruits and polarizes macrophages toward a pro-reparative M2 phenotype, while Arg fuels the arginase-1 metabolic pathway to sustain continual efferocytosis and secretion of pro-regenerative cytokines. In a mouse bone injury model, transcriptomic and histological analyses confirmed that this strategy accelerates apoptotic clearance and establishes an M2-dominant environment, significantly enhancing early bone regeneration. Altogether, this work proposes a novel therapeutic paradigm targeting macrophage efferocytosis to resolve early microenvironmental imbalances, providing a promising therapeutic approach to promote bone defect healing and offering novel insights into optimizing host microenvironments for osseointegration following implantation.

papers.title: Automatic Termination Strategy of Inelastic Neutron-scattering Measurement Using Bayesian Optimization for Bin-width Selection
papers.abstract: Currently, an excessive amount of event data is being obtained in four-dimensional inelastic neutron-scattering experiments. A method for automatic bin-width optimization of multidimensional histograms has been developed and recently validated on real inelastic neutron-scattering data. However, measuring beyond the equipment resolution leads to inefficient use of valuable beam time. To improve experimental efficiency, an automatic termination strategy is essential. We propose a Bayesian-optimization-based method to compute a stopping criterion that can support online decisions on whether to continue or terminate an experiment. In the proposed method, the bin-width optimization is performed using Bayesian optimization to efficiently compute the optimal bin widths. The experiment is terminated when the optimal bin widths become smaller than the target resolutions. In numerical experiments using real inelastic neutron-scattering data, the optimal bin widths decrease as the number of events increases. Even the optimal bin widths for data downsampled to 1/5 are comparable with the resolutions limited by the sample size, choppers, and so on. This implies excessive measurement of the inelastic neutron experiments for the moment. Moreover, we found that Bayesian optimization can reduce the search cost to approximately 10% of an exhaustive search in our numerical experiments.

papers.title: Volumetric Wear of Highly Cross-Linked Polyethylene Sockets in Total Hip Arthroplasty Differs Among Brands: A Retrieval Study
papers.abstract: Outcomes after total hip arthroplasty (THA) remain limited by wear and wear particle reaction. Although highly cross-linked polyethylene (HXLPE) mitigated this issue, there are major differences among the various brands available. This study quantified, for the first time, the volumetric wear on the retrievals from various HXLPE brands, using an optical coordinate measuring machine. Patient- and implant-related factors and component orientation were considered. As of 30.06.2025, 104 HXLPE sockets were available, and 79 could be analysed, excluding those too severely deformed/damaged. The median (range) time in situ was 8.7 (2.1–22.1) years. Wear volume and volumetric wear rate were 91 (1–674) mm3 and 9 (0–130) mm3/year, respectively. Highcross (n = 56, Medacta) experienced approximately five times more wear (p < 0.001) than Durasul (n = 17, Zimmer Biomet). The other brands (n = 6) were too small in group size at this stage for statistical analysis. The correlation (R2 = 0.94) between linear and volumetric wear was excellent, but high wearing retrievals had a strong impact on this analysis, whereas low wear retrievals showed high variability. Differences in wear were mostly driven by the brand, while other parameters had only a minor impact. This is the first retrieval study comparing volumetric wear among various brands of retrieved HXLPE bearings. Not all HXLPE bearings should be considered equal. As the cohort grows, further parameters and brands may be integrated.

papers.title: Stress-informed parametric shape adaptive patient-specific implant design in computer-assisted jaw reconstruction
papers.abstract: Introduction Reconstructing the jaw after tumor removal or trauma increasingly relies on custom 3D-printed titanium plates. This customization applies to the implant's shape. It usually does not apply to the internal structure. The width and thickness of the plate are still determined by the designer, based on experience and clinical observation. The critical design parameters of the PSI govern its mechanical performance. Hence, if the design could analyze these parameters and adjust them accordingly, it could help avoid plate fracture. This study introduces a parametric-design approach that closes this gap. Methods The proposed algorithm addresses these challenges by using stress data derived from finite element analysis (FEA) to selectively reinforce only the high-stress regions of a reconstruction plate, rather than uniformly reinforcing the entire plate. The reinforcement is smoothly integrated into the plate’s geometry to prevent abrupt changes in cross-section that could create stress concentrations. The approach was applied to a baseline plate at two regions of elevated stress. Results and discussion Plate A reinforced only the primary zone; this reduced peak stress by 36.0% and strain by 43.8% in that zone, the largest reduction observed across both design variants, and also lowered stress and strain in the second, unmodified zone by 12.7% and 14.3%, respectively. Plate B reinforced both zones; this further reduced stress and strain at the second zone by approximately 30.6% and 33.3%, respectively, and reduced strain at the primary zone by approximately 40.6% relative to baseline. Relative to Plate A, Plate B showed a slightly higher stress at the first zone; this stress remained well below the original baseline value. This work shows that patient-specific implant geometry can be shaped directly by biomechanical feedback. This algorithm offers an efficient computational workflow, enabling implants that are not only anatomically tailored but also mechanically optimized as per given loading conditions.

papers.title: A comprehensive evaluation of success rate and complications in pterygoid implant placement in posterior maxilla- a clinico-radiographic study
papers.abstract: BackgroundRehabilitation of the atrophic posterior maxilla remains a major challenge because of inadequate residual bone height, poor bone quality, and maxillary sinus pneumatization.Although sinus augmentation has traditionally been the treatment of choice, it increases surgical morbidity, treatment duration, and cost.Pterygoid implants provide a graftless alternative by engaging the dense cortical bone of the pterygoid process, allowing rehabilitation without sinus augmentation.Aim:To evaluate the clinical and radiographic success of pterygoid implant placement and assess postoperative complications in patients with atrophic posterior maxilla.Materials and Methods:A prospective clinico-radiographic study was conducted on 15 patients requiring implantsupported rehabilitation of the posterior maxilla.All patients underwent pterygoid implant placement using a standardized surgical protocol.Clinical parameters including pain, swelling, trismus, bleeding, infection, implant mobility, and other postoperative complications were evaluated at predetermined follow-up intervals.Radiographic assessment was performed to evaluate implant position, osseointegration, and peri-implant bone changes.Statistical analysis was performed using appropriate tests, with p < 0.05 considered statistically significant.Results:Fifteen patients successfully underwent pterygoid implant placement.Clinical evaluation demonstrated excellent implant stability throughout the follow-up period, with no implant mobility observed.Postoperative swelling and trismus showed progressive improvement, while bleeding resolved completely during follow-up.No cases of postoperative infection, oroantral fistula, implant fracture, or maxillary tuberosity fracture were recorded.Radiographic evaluation confirmed satisfactory implant positioning, successful osseointegration, and stable peri-implant bone levels, indicating a high clinical success rate.Conclusion:Pterygoid implants represent a predictable and effective graftless treatment modality for rehabilitation of the atrophic posterior maxilla.High implant stability, favorable radiographic outcomes, and a low complication rate support their use as a reliable alternative to sinus augmentation in appropriately selected patients.

papers.title: Research Progress on Offline Defect-Detection Technologies for Selective Laser-Melting Parts
papers.abstract: Selective laser melting (SLM) is recognized as one of the most promising metal additive manufacturing technologies for industrial deployment and has been applied to fabricate precision components for high-end equipment in sectors including aerospace and biomedicine. Nevertheless, ensuring reliable component quality and consistent performance remain a core challenge for SLM, which is widely acknowledged as a major barrier restricting the large-scale industrial application of the technology. Multi-scale and multi-type defects, which are difficult to fully suppress during the forming process, are the primary contributing factors to this issue. Accordingly, research on offline defect-detection technologies for SLM components is a critical pathway to break through the quality bottleneck and has emerged as a prominent research focus in both academia and industry. Based on a systematic review of relevant literature published in the past five years, this paper summarizes the morphological characteristics and formation mechanisms of typical defects in SLM-fabricated parts, including porosity, cracks, inclusions, and surface-forming defects. It elaborates on mainstream offline detection methods such as ultrasonic testing, X-ray computed tomography (XCT), and deep learning-enabled intelligent detection, and clarifies the respective performance advantages and inherent limitations of each technology. A quantitative comparison of these technologies is conducted from three core dimensions, detection accuracy, detection efficiency, and deployment cost, and differentiated application scenarios are defined corresponding to defect characteristics. Finally, the paper concludes with a full summary and prospects future in-depth research directions and industrial development trends in the field of SLM offline defect detection.

papers.title: Electromagnetic buffer optimization using multi-response grey hierarchical clustering
papers.abstract: Purpose This paper aims to optimize the structural parameters of a newly developed coaxial electromagnetic buffer of artillery that integrates an eddy-current recoil brake and a spring-type recuperator to achieve low-recoil and stable braking performance. Design/methodology/approach The dynamic equations governing the recoil and counter-recoil processes are formulated, followed by a finite element model incorporating the nonlinear hysteresis and temperature-dependent characteristics of NdFeB permanent magnets. Multi-response grey hierarchical clustering is then proposed to identify key structural parameters. Based on the screened design variables, a Kriging surrogate model is constructed, and a hybrid multi-objective optimization strategy combining the multi-island genetic algorithm and sequential quadratic programming is developed to determine the optimal structural design. Findings The finite element model achieves high prediction accuracy, with dynamic response errors below 5% under three charge conditions. The optimized design reduces the peak recoil resistance from 39.81 kN to 34.68 kN, representing a 12.89% reduction, while satisfying the prescribed recoil displacement constraint. Practical implications The proposed electromagnetic buffer provides an effective alternative to conventional hydraulic recoil systems. The physically validated finite element model and surrogate-based optimization framework can support the structural design and performance improvement of recoil mechanisms for artillery systems. Originality/value This work proposes a multi-response grey hierarchical clustering method for design-variable sensitivity analysis, enabling comprehensive variable screening by jointly accounting for their influence across multiple performance responses.

papers.title: Alignment restoration of the hip and the influence on outcomes following DAA THA in none-obese and obese patients: a retrospective comparative study
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Accurate biomechanical alignment is crucial for the success of Total Hip Arthroplasty (THA). Obesity poses an increasing challenge in THA. This study compares hip restoration and clinical outcomes after direct anterior approach (DAA) THA between non-obese and obese patients. Methods Biomechanical alignments after DAA THA were evaluated on postoperative radiographs by global, acetabular and femoral offsets as well as leg length and abductor lever arm. Restoration was calculated as the difference of the operated hip to the contralateral native joint (Δ). Precision was assessed using ± 5 mm and ± 2,5 mm target zones. Significant alignment parameters influencing clinical outcomes were evaluated using one-year postoperative WOMAC scores and compared between obese (BMI ≥ 30 kg/cm 2 ) and non-obese (BMI < 30 kg/cm 2 ) patients. Results No significant differences in biomechanical restoration ( N = 494) were found between obese and non-obese patients. Precision within the ± 5 mm target zones ranged from 31,4% to 73,5%, while precision within the ± 2,5 mm target zone ranged from 12,1% to 35,8%. Precision was independent of BMI. The abductor lever arm (ALA) alignment was the only radiographic parameter that correlated with clinical outcome ( N = 344). In the non-obese, the one-year postoperative WOMAC score was significantly better when ΔALA was ≥ 0 mm ( p = 0.023). However, this correlation was not observed in obese patients ( p > 0.05). In obese patients, WOMAC scores were significantly better when ΔALA was ≥ 2 mm ( p = 0.003). Conclusion Accuracy of biomechanical restoration following DAA THA is comparable in non-obese and obese patients. To improve clinical outcomes, reduction of ΔALA should be avoided; obese patients may even benefit from a slight increase of ΔALA.

papers.title: Digital Twin Modeling and Multi-Fidelity Deep Surrogate Simulation of Corrosion Fatigue Degradation Processes for the Condition-Based Maintenance of Permanent Flexible Fall Arrest Systems
papers.abstract: Permanent flexible fall arrest systems are safety-critical equipment whose load-bearing capacity is governed by two coupled processes acting on very different time scales: a millisecond-scale transient arrest process and a multi-year corrosion fatigue degradation process. This paper develops a digital twin framework that represents both processes within a single simulation and monitoring architecture, so that the condition of an in-service system is inferred from its actual state rather than from installation design parameters. The flexible horizontal lifeline is described by a geometrically nonlinear cable formulation in which sag, pretension, and large displacement during arrest are retained, while corrosion and cyclic loading enter as time-varying parameters of the effective cross-sectional area and the residual strength. To remove the computational bottleneck of repeated high-fidelity finite element evaluation over the service horizon, a multi-fidelity deep surrogate is built from a low-fidelity analytical solver and a small set of high-fidelity simulations, with transfer learning correcting the systematic bias of the coarse model and recovering the sharp peak of the arrest force. The surrogate is then embedded in a Bayesian state updating loop driven by periodic inspection data. Across quasi-static, dynamic arrest, and long-term degradation case studies, it reproduces the peak arrest force and the anchor reaction within about 3.5% of the high-fidelity reference, reduces the evaluation time by several orders of magnitude, and tracks the residual fatigue life under realistic inspection intervals. All reference values here come from the high-fidelity model developed in this paper, with no physical test or field record, so the work is reported as a proof-of-concept framework rather than a validated engineering tool, indicating a candidate route toward condition-based maintenance planning of fall protection infrastructure.

papers.title: Cementless total hip arthroplasty in patients ≤ 25 years: favorable survivorship and clinical outcomes at medium-term follow-up
papers.abstract: Abstract Objective This study evaluated the medium-term clinical and radiographic results of cementless total hip arthroplasty (THA) in patients aged 25 years or younger. Methods This retrospective cohort study included 37 patients (49 hips) who underwent cementless THA between 2009 and 2020. The mean patient age at surgery was 21.8 years, and the mean follow-up duration was 10.2 years (range, 4.8-16.2 years). Clinical outcomes were assessed using patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs), including the modified Harris Hip Score (mHHS), the Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Osteoarthritis Index (WOMAC), and the 36-Item Short-Form Health Survey (SF-36). Radiographic evaluations focused on implant positioning, leg length discrepancy (LLD), signs of loosening, bearing surface wear, periprosthetic osteolysis, and heterotopic ossification. Postoperative complications and revision surgeries were also documented. Results All PROMs demonstrated statistically significant improvements postoperatively. The mHHS increased from 44.6 to 88.6. The WOMAC score decreased from 42.9 to 7.5. The SF-36 Physical Component Score improved from 48.5 to 81.2, and the Mental Component Score increased from 56.6 to 82.6. Radiographically, optimal implant positioning was achieved, with a mean acetabular inclination of 40.1° and anteversion of 14.2°. LLD was significantly reduced from 0.9 cm to 0.2 cm. Complications included two dislocations, two cases of transient neuropraxia (in patients diagnosed with developmental dysplasia of the hip), and one periprosthetic joint infection treated with debridement, antibiotics, and implant retention (DAIR) plus acetabular liner exchange; because the liner was exchanged, this procedure was counted as a revision event. Periprosthetic osteolysis was observed in five hips (10.2%), but no cases of progressive osteolysis, loosening, or detectable wear were detected. The 10-year implant survivorship was 98.0%. All improvements exceeded the minimal clinically important difference (MCID) thresholds reported for these instruments. Conclusion In this cohort of young patients (≤25 years) without prior hip infection, cementless THA provided substantial clinical improvement, favorable radiographic outcomes, and high implant survivorship at medium-term follow-up, with a low revision rate.

papers.title: Equivalent force-based Kalman-type filter and reduced system function for full-field response reconstruction
papers.abstract: Abstract In structural health monitoring, full-field response sensing and monitoring are essential to establish a digital twin model. However, directly measuring all required structural loads and responses is costly and impractical. Simultaneous estimations of structural loads and responses are consequently developed, which is, however, an ill-posed problem. This paper aims to address the ill-posed nature of the simultaneous estimation of load and response from insufficient observations, which is realized by reducing the dimension of unknown loads via principal component analysis to derive the equivalent system functions. First, a set of force basis vectors is calculated from the structural impulse responses in a single time step to replace the original load vector. Subsequently, a reduced equivalent system model is obtained with sufficient controllability on the original system model. Then, the equivalent loads and full-field responses can be simultaneously estimated by the Kalman-type joint input-state estimation filters. The proposed technique is applied to a numerical beam model and a real long-span sea-crossing bridge under operational traffic and typhoon loads. Results show that the full-field responses to arbitrarily distributed and unknown loads are correctly reconstructed from noisy data.

papers.title: Nanoporous titanium implant functionalized with sustained strontium release orchestrates immune microenvironment for enhanced osseointegration
papers.abstract: Objectives Insufficient osseointegration remains a major limitation of dental and orthopedic implants. This study aimed to develop a strontium-releasing nanoporous titanium surface (TDS) with improved interfacial stability and immunomodulatory capacity to promote implant osseointegration. Methods A nanoporous titanium surface was fabricated by anodization and selected over a nanotube structure because of its greater interfacial stability. Polydopamine-mediated coordination was then used to immobilize strontium on the nanoporous surface. Surface properties and strontium release were characterized. Macrophage polarization and the effects of the TDS-modulated immune microenvironment on osteogenic differentiation of mouse bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (mBMSCs) and angiogenic activity of human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) were evaluated in vitro. Additional experiments were performed to assess the direct effects of TDS on osteogenic and angiogenic responses. Osseointegration was examined in a rat femoral condyle defect model, and macrophage transcriptomic profiling was conducted. Results TDS retained a uniform nanoporous morphology, showed favorable hydrophilicity, and provided sustained strontium release. It promoted macrophage polarization toward the anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype and reduced pro-inflammatory responses. The TDS-modulated immune microenvironment significantly enhanced osteogenic differentiation and angiogenic activity, while direct material effects provided additional support. In vivo experiments further confirmed satisfactory osseointegration in bone defect areas after TDS implantation for 4 and 8 weeks. Transcriptomic analysis identified gene expression changes associated with immune regulation, inflammatory responses, and angiogenesis. Conclusions Overall, this study provides experimental evidence and a practical design strategy for the development of immunomodulatory titanium implants with improved osseointegration.

papers.title: Novel Surrogate-Assisted Structural Optimization Framework for Full-Aircraft Configurations
papers.abstract: Designing lighter aircraft structures while satisfying strength, stability, and aeroelastic requirements remains a central challenge in preliminary aircraft design. Many early-stage aircraft structural optimization studies rely on beam, equivalent-plate, or semi-empirical structural representations, while many higher-fidelity studies focus on isolated components, particularly wings, rather than the simultaneous sizing of the wing, fuselage, and tail within a unified structural model. The present study addresses this gap by introducing a surrogate-assisted structural optimization framework for complete aircraft configurations. The framework is built around a fully parametric shell/beam-based finite element model of a representative long-range transport aircraft configuration with a high-aspect-ratio wing, coupled to aerodynamic loads computed using the subsonic source and doublet panel method. The proposed framework allows simultaneous sizing of the wing, fuselage, and tail under static strength, global buckling, and flutter constraints, while retaining a computational cost suitable for preliminary design studies. The optimization results are assessed through three independent surrogate-assisted optimization runs initialized from different sampling distributions and compared to a derivative-free optimization solver using the same computational budget. The independent runs identify feasible low-mass configurations with consistent convergence trends. The optimized design gives a full-aircraft modeled mass of 230.48 t, which remains below the reference maximum takeoff mass of 268 t and is consistent with the expected mass scale of representative long-range transport aircraft. Overall, the proposed framework provides a practical preliminary-design tool for exploring feasible full-aircraft structural layouts, identifying dominant load paths and active constraints, and generating candidate designs for subsequent higher-fidelity aeroelastic and certification-level refinement.

papers.title: Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Stress Analysis in In-Plane Crack Problems
papers.abstract: Abstract Accurate prediction of stress fields near crack tips is essential for failure analysis in structural materials, but remains challenging due to the 1/ √ r singular nature of the solution in linear elastic fracture mechanics (LEFM). Finite element methods (FEM) require strong mesh refinement near cracks and demand high computational costs and times for accurate stress analysis. Alternatively, standard neural networks fail to capture the important asymptotic behavior, producing poor predictions in the near-tip process region even when achieving excellent far-field accuracy. We present an enriched Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) framework for reconstructing stress distributions for in-plane crack problems by embedding the Williams Mode-I asymptotic displacement field directly into the network architecture. Evaluated on Abaqus finite element reference solutions for AA2050 and Fe 50 Mn 30 Co 10 Cr 10 high-entropy alloy in a single-edge notched tension configuration, the enriched PINN achieves near-tip R 2 of 0.902 (σ 11 ) and 0.912 (σ 22 ). The framework maintains competitive far-field accuracy as well (R 2 > 0.990) and produces instantaneous stress field evaluations after training. The enriched PINN successfully captures the near-tip singularity and reconstructs the global stress field while generalizing across materials.

papers.title: XCoM-Based Moving-Mass Control in a Backpack for Modulating Gait Stability During Load Carriage
papers.abstract: Backpack load carriage can alter gait mechanics and dynamic stability, while existing assistive backpacks have primarily targeted load transmission and metabolic cost. This study investigated whether active vertical repositioning of a moving mass within a backpack could influence gait-stability-related outcomes. A frontal-plane double inverted pendulum model was combined with inertial measurement unit (IMU)-derived motion states to calculate a model-estimated mediolateral extrapolated center of mass (XCoM), and model predictive control (MPC) regulated a 5 kg moving mass in real time. Six participants walked on a treadmill at 1.2 m/s under a Normal condition, three fixed-mass conditions (Low, Mid, and High), and a Powered condition with XCoM-based moving-mass control. Short-term largest Lyapunov exponent (LLE), kinematic variability (KV), and trunk sway were evaluated as gait-stability-related outcomes. In the Powered condition, short-term LLE was 19.0%, 15.7%, and 24.4% lower than in the Low, Mid, and High conditions, respectively, with all six participants showing lower LLE in each comparison. However, no pairwise comparison of LLE, KV, or trunk sway remained statistically significant after Bonferroni correction. The model-estimated XCoM and filtered moving-mass velocity command were negatively correlated (r=−0.3310). These findings support the feasibility of state-dependent moving-mass control during load carriage and indicate the need for further evaluation of its effects on gait stability in a larger cohort.

papers.title: Acetabular-only robot-assisted total hip arthroplasty is associated with lower surgeon stress index and perceived workload than conventional total hip arthroplasty: a prospective comparative cohort study
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Robot-assisted THA (RATHA) has been associated with greater component-positioning accuracy, but surgeon workload during RATHA remains unclear. This study compared objective physiologic stress and perceived workload during conventional THA (CTHA) and RATHA. METHODS: This exploratory, hypothesis-generating study prospectively evaluated 60 elective primary THAs, comprising 30 CTHAs and 30 RATHAs, as repeated procedural observations from a single high-volume, fellowship-trained arthroplasty surgeon. All procedures were performed through a standardized posterolateral approach. RATHA used the MAKO system for acetabular preparation and cup implantation only. Intraoperative physiologic data were collected using a Hexoskin smart garment. Whole-case outcomes included heart rate, stress index, root mean square of successive differences (RMSSD), respiratory rate, minute ventilation, and energy expenditure rate. Perceived workload was assessed using the Surgery Task Load Index (SURG-TLX). Phase-specific stress index and RMSSD were analyzed across exposure, acetabular preparation, femoral preparation, and wound closure. RESULTS: Baseline patient characteristics were comparable between groups. Operative time was significantly longer during RATHA than CTHA (141.50 ± 30.76 vs 116.86 ± 21.88 min, p < 0.001). Despite this, RATHA was associated with a lower SURG-TLX composite score (adjusted mean difference, - 0.47; 95% CI - 0.85 to - 0.09; p = 0.039), with lower scores for task complexity and situational stress. Whole-case stress index was lower during RATHA (adjusted mean difference, - 2.52; 95% CI - 4.21 to - 0.83; p = 0.004), whereas the between-group difference in whole-case RMSSD was not statistically significant (geometric mean ratio, 1.35; 95% CI 0.98-1.86; p = 0.067). Heart rate, respiratory rate, minute ventilation, and energy expenditure rate did not differ significantly between groups. Phase-specific analysis showed lower stress index during RATHA in exposure, acetabular preparation, and femoral preparation, but higher stress index during wound closure. RMSSD was higher during RATHA in exposure and acetabular preparation. CONCLUSIONS: In this single-surgeon cohort, the acetabular-only RATHA workflow was associated with lower perceived workload and a lower mean whole-case stress index than the CTHA workflow despite longer operative time. These hypothesis-generating findings warrant validation in multisurgeon studies.

papers.title: Effects of Training Data Source on PINN Modeling of Laser-Induced Heat Diffusion in Human Skin
papers.abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) have recently emerged as an effective surrogate to classical numerical methods for solving partial differential equations (PDEs) in a wide range of physical systems. When augmented with supervised data, PINN performance can depend strongly on the quality and characteristics of the training data; however, the influence of the numerical method used to generate that data remains largely unexplored. In this study, we investigate how training data generated by finite difference method (FDM) and finite element method (FEM) solvers affects PINN training and predictive accuracy, particularly in solving the one-dimensional heat equation under conditions relevant to laser–tissue interactions. A supervised data loss term is incorporated, and models trained on FDM- and FEM-generated temperature fields under identical physical conditions are compared to assess differences in convergence and accuracy. The results demonstrate that, under controlled one-dimensional diffusion settings, the numerical solver used for data generation produces a quantifiable, resolution-dependent effect on hybrid PINN performance: FDM-generated training data yields the lowest error across most tested resolutions, an advantage that narrows and becomes indistinguishable only at the finest resolution considered, providing practical guidance for selecting a data-generating solver in biological heat transfer applications.

papers.title: Egg White-Based Biomaterials: Morphological Architectures and Emerging Biomedical Applications
papers.abstract: Egg white (EW) has emerged as a versatile natural biomaterial due to its wide availability, low cost, biodegradability, intrinsic bioactivity, and protein-derived gel- and film-forming capabilities. However, the existing literature has largely addressed EW-based biomaterials in terms of individual fabrication methods or specific applications, while comprehensive evaluations linking processing strategies to the resulting morphology, physicochemical properties, and biomedical functions remain limited. In this review, EW-based biomaterials are critically evaluated through an integrated processing, structure, property, and function framework encompassing molecular composition, fabrication strategies, morphological organization, physicochemical behavior, and biomedical performance. The molecular interactions and processing-dependent structural changes in major EW proteins, including ovalbumin, ovotransferrin, ovomucoid, ovomucin, and lysozyme, are discussed, and physical gelation, chemical and enzymatic crosslinking, chemical functionalization, and polymer/nanomaterial hybridization are compared as major fabrication approaches. These strategies enable the development of diverse morphologies, including hydrogels, nano/microparticles, films and membranes, micro/nanofibers, porous sponges, cryogels, and 3D-printed constructs, which provide distinct functional advantages in tissue engineering, 3D cell culture, wound healing, drug and bioactive molecule delivery, bioprinting, and biosensing. Particular emphasis is placed on the roles of crosslink density, porosity, swelling behavior, mechanical properties, degradation, and molecular transport in governing cellular responses and overall biomedical performance. Despite these advantages, batch-to-batch variability, the limited mechanical robustness of native protein networks, sterilization and storage constraints, and potential allergenicity and immunogenicity remain major barriers to clinical translation. Future research should therefore focus on standardized protein formulations, application-specific hybrid networks, advanced biofabrication approaches, and comprehensive long-term biosafety studies to enhance the translational potential of EW-based biomaterials.

papers.title: Mechanical behavior and weight reduction of titanium frameworks with topology‐optimized lattice structures for implant‐supported prostheses
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: This study aimed to investigate the mechanical behavior of titanium frameworks with triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) lattice structures designed for additive manufacturing by topology optimization for complete arch implant-supported fixed dental prostheses. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A maxillary model supported by four implants (two posteriorly tilted and two anterior parallel) was virtually modeled using a dental computer-aided design program. Titanium frameworks for complete arch implant-supported fixed dental prostheses, which incorporated three distinct TPMS lattice structures (Schwarz, Diamond, and Lidinoid) with variable cell wall thicknesses, were designed using topology optimization software. A total of 36 optimized framework designs were analyzed by finite element analysis under vertical and oblique loading (200 N) at the canine, premolar, and molar (cantilever) regions. A solid, non-optimized titanium framework was the control group. von Mises stress (MPa), maximum displacement (µm), reaction forces (N), and weight reduction ratios (%) were analyzed. Statistical analyses were performed with ANOVA and Tukey's post hoc test (α = 0.05). RESULTS: All topology-optimized frameworks achieved >30% weight reduction, with the Diamond lattice structure demonstrating the highest reduction of 39.92 ± 2.60 (p < 0.001). Although optimized frameworks exhibited higher displacement and stress values than solid controls because of increased flexibility, the peak stress values (190-210 MPa) remained significantly below the yield strength of titanium. Optimized frameworks generated significantly lower reaction forces than solid controls under canine and premolar loading, indicating an energy-absorbing effect. CONCLUSIONS: Topology optimization created a semi-rigid framework that incorporates the shock-absorbing benefits of polymers while maintaining the inherent fracture resistance of metallic alloys. Topology-optimized titanium frameworks provide a clinically viable solution for reducing prosthetic weight and minimizing reaction forces at the abutment interface, particularly in complete-arch rehabilitations.

papers.title: Physics-informed neural operators for rapid electric field prediction in transcranial magnetic stimulation of healthy and tumor subjects
papers.abstract: Accurate and rapid prediction of transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS)-induced electric fields is essential for personalized clinical applications, from individualized therapy in major depressive disorder to presurgical functional mapping in neuro-oncology. Yet conventional finite element methods are often too computationally expensive for interactive use. Existing deep learning surrogate models partly address this limitation but are largely constrained to fixed voxel-grid representations that cannot naturally accommodate the irregular geometry of subject-specific head meshes. We present the first physics-informed neural operator (PINO) for subject-specific prediction of vector TMS electric fields, built on a mesh-native dual-encoder architecture that jointly encodes head anatomy and coil configuration. By incorporating a curl-based regularization term aligned with the curl-free nature of the TMS secondary field, the PINO model promotes physical consistency as a soft regularizer alongside data-driven supervision. Trained on 75 subjects from the IXI dataset, the framework was evaluated across four independent held-out test datasets, including healthy subjects from two additional MRI cohorts and, for the first time in learning-based TMS electric-field prediction, tumor patients. The resolution-agnostic formulation generalizes across subjects, coil types, and spatial resolutions without retraining, predicting vector electric fields on approximately 300,000 gray matter volume nodes in under 100 ms on a consumer-grade GPU. Across all test datasets within the focality-50% region, the PINO model achieved median center-of-gravity errors of 0.39–0.43 mm, RMSE of 0.12–0.16 V/m, and mean angular deviations of 6.7°–7.3°, with performance within or below the error ranges reported by recent deep-learning approaches. At the selected 5% physics-loss weighting, curl loss decreased by 9.1% relative to the data-only model, while RMSE and MAD increased by only 1.6% and 1.3%, respectively. These results suggest that physics-informed neural operators provide a scalable technical foundation for rapid gray-matter electric-field approximation, supporting future studies on real-time electric-field-guided TMS workflows

papers.title: Finite element model updating in extradosed cable-stayed bridges using the RSM-MPSO method
papers.abstract: Accurate finite element (FE) models serve as the foundation for assessing the structural condition of bridges. To establish a high-fidelity FE model capable of precisely characterising the static and dynamic behaviours of an extradosed cable-stayed bridge, this study proposes a collaborative optimisation framework integrating response surface methodology and a modified particle swarm optimisation algorithm, achieving efficient and high-precision model parameter calibration. Through experimental design and sensitivity analysis, critical parameters influencing structural responses were identified, and a response surface surrogate model was developed for iterative computation. A comprehensive objective function was formulated by incorporating field-measured data, and the improved particle swarm optimisation algorithm was employed to iteratively optimise the objective function, thereby obtaining precise FE model parameters. Results demonstrate that the response surface surrogate model, based on sensitivity analysis, achieved correlation coefficients exceeding 0.96 with root mean square error approaching zero. The maximum relative error on the displacement at critical girder cross-sections decreased from 31.40% to 11.62%, and the average relative error reduced from 28.97% to 9.89%. In addition, the mean relative error of the first five natural frequencies decreased from 16.21% to 5.80%, confirming that the updated FE model accurately simulates the actual structural response.

papers.title: In-vitro Evaluation of 3D Bioprinted Alginate Membranes for Periodontal Regeneration: Mechanical Properties, Biocompatibility and Drug Release Analysis
papers.abstract: Introduction: Alginate-based hydrogel membranes are commonly used in periodontal applications due to their biocompatibility. Rosuvastatin (RSV), a lipid lowering drug is known for inducing osteoblastic differentiation by several studies. Aim: To assess the physical properties {using Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM), Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR), surface roughness, and contact angle} and drug release behaviour (via Franz Diffusion Method) of alginate-based 3D bioprinted membranes, with and without 1.2% RSV. Materials and Methods: This in-vitro study was conducted in Department of Periodontology, Sri Ramachandra Dental College and Hospital, Chennai, Tamil Nadu, India from September 2025 to November 2025. Two bioinks, including one with 1.2% RSV and other premade bioink CELLINK BONE®, were 3D printed into 10 mm × 10 mm × 1 mm membranes. Each bioink was incorporated with RSV calcium (18 mg - CELLINK BONE® and 12 mg - 6% Alginate). Membranes were printed in rectilinear and honeycomb patterns and crosslinked using 0.5% Calcium chloride. Physical properties, haemocompatibility and drug release were then evaluated. Results: SEM and FTIR analysis validated the formation and typical morphology of the 6% alginate membranes. The membranes were hydrophilic and haemocompatible, while the one with RSV had sustained drug release. However, the CELLINK BONE® membrane loaded with RSV was not structurally stable as it disintegrated after processing. Conclusion: The results indicate that both membranes are promising for their use in Guided Tissue Regeneration (GTR), serving as scaffolds as well as local drug delivery systems.

papers.title: Sparse measurement correction for full-field displacement prediction of nonlinear structures using reduced-order models and Gaussian process regression
papers.abstract: Online full-field displacement reconstruction from sparse measurements is an important task in nonlinear structural analysis, monitoring, and digital-twin applications. Direct finite element simulations are often too expensive for repeated online use, whereas input-only reduced-order model–Gaussian process regression (ROM-GPR) surrogate models may produce biased full-field predictions when the target structural state is insufficiently represented by offline training data. Sparse displacement measurements provide current-state information, but observation-only reconstruction is usually underdetermined or noise-sensitive under limited sensing conditions. To address this issue, this work develops a probabilistic correction strategy for ROM-GPR full-field displacement predictions by statistically weighting the input-informed surrogate estimate and sparse measurements according to their respective uncertainties. The Gaussian process regression (GPR) prediction provides a low-dimensional estimate with quantified regression uncertainty, while the measurement constraint uses an observation error covariance that accounts for sensor noise and the observation-space projection of reduced-order reconstruction residuals. Sparse measurements are incorporated through an error-covariance-weighted correction in the reduced-order space, with the ensemble Kalman filter (EnKF) and unscented Kalman filter (UKF) adopted as sampling-based implementations. Tests on two nonlinear 2D finite element examples and a 3D liver model show that the proposed correction reduces the mean reconstruction error by 55.92%–73.51% for autoencoder-based ROM-GPR and 72.48%–93.10% for proper orthogonal decomposition-based ROM-GPR.

papers.title: A neural operator framework for data-driven discovery of stability and receptivity in physical systems
papers.abstract: Understanding how complex systems respond to perturbations, such as whether they will remain stable or what their most sensitive patterns are, is a fundamental challenge across science and engineering. Traditional stability and receptivity (resolvent) analyses are powerful but rely on known equations and linearization, limiting their use in nonlinear or poorly modeled systems. Here, we introduce a data-driven framework that automatically identifies stability properties of both equilibrium points and periodic orbits, as well as optimal forcing responses from observation data alone, without requiring governing equations. By training a neural network as a dynamics emulator and using automatic differentiation to extract its Jacobian, we can perform stability and receptivity analyses directly from data. We demonstrate the method on systems of increasing complexity, from canonical models to high-dimensional fluid flows and a real-world climate dataset, employing model reduction where needed and successfully identifying dominant instability modes and optimal input–output structures, even in strongly nonlinear regimes. By leveraging a neural network emulator, we readily obtain a nonlinear representation of system dynamics while additionally retrieving intricate dynamical patterns that were previously difficult to resolve. This equation-free methodology establishes a broadly applicable tool for analyzing complex, high-dimensional datasets, with potential relevance to grand challenges in fields such as climate science, neuroscience, and fluid engineering.

papers.title: Probabilistic Digital Twin Framework for Climate-Resilient Offshore Infrastructure under Coupled Corrosion–Fatigue Degradation and Environmental Uncertainty
papers.abstract: Offshore assets deteriorate through mechanisms that reinforce one another: corrosion removes section and raises the local stress, the elevated stress accelerates fatigue, and fatigue damage exposes fresh metal to the marine environment. Deterministic integrity assessment cannot represent that feedback or the environmental variability that drives it. This paper presents a physics-informed probabilistic digital twin for offshore infrastructure in which coupled corrosion–fatigue degradation modelling, Monte Carlo uncertainty propagation, sequential Bayesian data assimilation and a physics-constrained neural surrogate are combined within a single lifecycle assessment loop. The degradation state is a bounded composite index of corrosion penetration, Miner fatigue damage, cumulative environmental exposure and an interaction component, with the stress-amplification coupling regularised so that no governing relation becomes singular as failure is approached. Structural performance is tracked through the second-moment reliability index, and the Infrastructure Degradation Instability Index (IDII) is defined as a bounded, dimensionless ratio between an instability driver, the product of normalised degradation rate and dispersion, and the normalised reliability margin. For a 32 mm-wall tubular reference component configured deliberately as an aggressive 30-year demonstration case, the reliability index falls from 3.48 to 0.70 and the target of 1.5 is reached at 17.8 years; the empirical failure probability counted from the 30,000 Monte Carlo limit-state samples differs from Φ(−β) by at most 2.2 × 10−4, so the two-moment approximation is verified rather than assumed. Global variance decomposition attributes 87 % of the variance in end-of-life degradation to environmental severity. Raising the environment-driven variability multiplier from 0.5 to 2.0 at constant mean severity advances the reliability-target year from 21.5 to 10.8 even though the mean degradation trajectory falls, so variability acts through dispersion rather than through the mean. Sequential importance resampling of annual thickness and strain measurements reduces the predictive dispersion of the 30-year degradation state by 81.5%. IDII thresholds of 0.15, 0.35, 0.50 and 0.65 are mapped to reliability-index levels of 3.06, 2.26, 1.71 and 1.05, and a 21-case sensitivity study shows that the composite-index weights move the reliability-target year between 15.9 and 19.3 years while leaving the regime ordering and the warning lead time (6.6–8.1 years) essentially unchanged. The surrogate reproduces held-out trajectories with RMSE 0.0078 and R2 0.999 but is unreliable beyond its training horizon, which is why long-horizon inference is carried by the Bayesian filter. All parameters, distributions and hyperparameters are reported; the framework is presented as probabilistic decision support for a demonstration configuration, with field validation identified as the prerequisite for operational use.

papers.title: Temperature-Field Reconstruction and Heat-Source Inversion Estimation Method for High-Voltage Switchgear Based Reduced-Order PINN Surrogate Model
papers.abstract: Abstract Localized overheating induced by poor electrical contact, loosened busbar connections, and insulation degradation is a major precursor to failures in high-voltage switchgear. To address the difficulty in directly measuring internal heat sources, a fast three-dimensional temperature-field reconstruction, candidate heat-source identification, and heat-source power inversion method for high-voltage switchgear is proposed based on a reduced-order surrogate model integrating Proper Orthogonal Decomposition (POD) and physics-informed neural networks (PINNs). First, a coupled three-dimensional thermal–flow coupled computational fluid dynamics(CFD) model is established to generate temperature fields under different heat-source conditions. POD is then applied to extract the dominant thermal modes and their corresponding low-dimensional modal coefficients from the high-dimensional temperature fields. A PINN-based reduced-order surrogate model is subsequently trained to establish the nonlinear mapping from heat-source parameters to POD modal coefficients, while residuals of the steady-state heat conduction equation and boundary-condition constraints are incorporated into the loss function to enforce physical consistency and enhance prediction accuracy. Based on external temperature measurements, an Improved Grey Wolf Optimizer (I-GWO) is further adopted to identify the active fault heat source from a predefined set of candidate locations and inversely estimate its corresponding heat-source power. Numerical simulations and temperature-rise experiments show that the proposed method accurately reconstructs the three-dimensional temperature distribution and identifies local high-temperature regions. In the temperature-rise experiment, the relative error of heat-source power inversion is only 2.27%, demonstrating that the proposed framework enables rapid and accurate temperature-field reconstruction and heat-source inversion.

papers.title: Ultra-broadband highly efficient sound absorption of MPP-TPMS composite acoustic metamaterial with multi-stage impedance matching
papers.abstract: Abstract Broadband and low-frequency noise control is highly demanded in advanced engineering fields such as aerospace and precision manufacturing. However, traditional sound-absorbing materials struggle to balance lightweight, high strength, and excellent low-frequency dissipation. In this paper, a novel "Micro-perforated Panel-Gyroid" (MPP-Gyroid) composite multifunctional acoustic metamaterial is proposed. First, JCA-TMM analytical models for Gyroid sound absorption and transmission loss were established and validated via thermionics simulations. To overcome the low-frequency limits of pure Gyroid lattices, a cascaded MPP-air cavity configuration was developed, with its non-convex impedance parameters globally optimized using Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The optimized results show that the effective absorption band is significantly broadened to 260–4610 Hz, with an average absorption coefficient of 0.93. Furthermore, by establishing a four-stage parallel array system optimized across sub-bands, the local Fabry-Perot resonance valleys were flattened utilizing transverse evanescent wave coupling at the fluid-solid interface. Ultimately, near-perfect sound absorption (α≥0.9) was achieved across an ultra-broadband range of 10–6000 Hz. This study elucidates the multi-scale acoustic energy dissipation mechanism of "low-frequency long-range penetration and high-frequency shallow interception," providing a new theoretical framework and engineering paradigm for the sophisticated design of load-bearing acoustic metamaterials.

papers.title: Conformal Risk-Calibrated Latent World Models with Runtime Assurance Under Distribution Shift
papers.abstract: Learning-enabled autonomous controllers may fail when a compact world model remains confident outside its training distribution. We present the conformal disagreement-regulated latent world model (CDR-LWM). The method converts ensemble disagreement into a risk-calibrated, state-dependent uncertainty radius for robust-envelope model predictive control. A split-conformal score scales next-state residuals by ensemble dispersion. A runtime governor then replaces the planned action with a stabilizing backup when the predicted envelope approaches a safety boundary or the ensemble novelty exceeds its empirical nominal quantile. We evaluated CartPole and torque-limited Pendulum stabilization using 15,000 locally generated transitions per task. The protocol used episode-disjoint fitting, calibration, and validation partitions, together with eight paired held-out seeds under nominal, dynamics, actuator, and observation conditions. Under Pendulum actuator shift, CDR-LWM reduced unsafe steps from 7.3% to 0% and episode failures from 50.0% to 0% while intervening on 9.3% of steps. Under dynamics shift, unsafe steps decreased from 14.9% to 7.4%, and episode failures decreased from 62.5% to 12.5%, with a 30.0% intervention rate. Under CartPole observation noise, CDR-LWM completed every evaluation episode without an unsafe state, whereas nominal MPC had a 37.5% episode-failure rate. Nominal one-step joint coverage was 0.909 for CartPole and 0.882 for Pendulum. Trigger-isolating ablations showed that novelty-triggered switching produced most of the closed-loop improvement. These results provide a compact and auditable link between calibrated model disagreement and selective runtime assurance under the evaluated shifts.

papers.title: The PROMES Regional Climate Model: Three Decades of Development and Contributions to Regional Climate Ensemble Research
papers.abstract: Regional climate models (RCMs) have become established as essential dynamical downscaling tools, providing physically consistent, high-resolution climate information where global climate models (GCMs) are unable to resolve. Added value is obtained over heterogeneous vegetation, coastal, urban or orographically complex zones. Temperature, precipitation or wind benefit whenever fine-scale processes govern the climate signal, as with extreme events. CORDEX initiative (since 2009) has further consolidated RCM research with coordinated multi-model ensembles covering all continental regions, enabling systematic uncertainty quantification of regional climate projections. PROMES RCM has been an active scientific contributor across three decades to the modelling community ensemble, with operations discontinued around 2015. This retrospective narrative review synthesizes and documents PROMES’s development, performance across Europe, West Africa and South America, and assesses its scientific contributions. This includes climate change projection features, extreme events (droughts, heat waves, or Mediterranean tropical-like cyclones) or land surface–atmosphere studies. Its behaviour within the more relevant international multi-model ensembles (from PRUDENCE to EuroCORDEX), with structurally independent characteristics, represents a scientific asset for uncertainty characterization beyond the model’s individual results, offering a legacy argument for preserving RCM diversity in ensemble design strategies, as it is an essential and many times underappreciated key point of uncertainty analysis.

papers.title: Process-Inspired Latent Dynamics for Direct Multi-Step Regional Sea Surface Temperature Forecasting
papers.abstract: Sea surface temperature (SST) forecasts support marine environmental monitoring, hazard assessment, and operational ocean services. Regional multi-step prediction remains difficult because SST-only models must represent transport, spatial spreading, and local nonlinear variation from historical fields while avoiding the recursive use of predicted states. We propose ADR-Net, a direct multi-step forecasting model that combines a flexible data-driven stream with a process-inspired advection–diffusion–reaction (ADR) stream in a shared latent bottleneck. The ADR stream organizes latent SST evolution through three operators that represent transport-like displacement, spatial spreading, and local nonlinear variation. A temporal projection module (TPM) then projects the fused latent representation and multi-scale encoder features directly to all forecast leads. We evaluated ADR-Net against eight learned baselines and two non-learned references using daily OISST v2.1 data from the East China Sea (ECS), South China Sea (SCS), Niño 1+2, and Niño 3.4 regions. Separate models were trained with output lengths L∈{1,7,13}. ADR-Net achieved the lowest MSE, MAE, and RMSE in all 12 region–output length settings across four regions and three output lengths. In the ECS, it reduced the MSE by 1.46%, 8.07%, and 5.70% relative to the best MSE baseline for L=1, L=7, and L=13, respectively. For the ECS L=13 task, ADR-Net maintained the lowest MAE and highest SSIM at every lead day and extended the mean effective forecast horizon from 3.91 to 4.49 days under grid cell thresholds of RMSE ≤ 0.7 °C and R2≥0.95. Component ablations on the ECS seven-day task showed that removing the TPM or the process-inspired ADR stream increased the mean MSE by 4.55% and 3.86%, respectively, while removing both increased it by 8.32%. ADR-Net used 7.09 million parameters and 13.07 GFLOPs per ECS seven-day forecast sample. Across four storm-associated episodes, ADR-Net achieved the lowest event-mean cooling footprint MAE at every forecast lead from day 1 to day 13. Together, these results support the combination of process-inspired latent modeling and direct temporal projection for accurate, spatially coherent regional SST forecasting.

papers.title: Expert Consensus on Robot-Assisted Vascularized Bone Grafting for the Treatment of Early-Stage Osteonecrosis of the Femoral Head
papers.abstract: Osteonecrosis of the femoral head (ONFH) remains a progressive clinical challenge that predominantly affects young and active adults between 20 and 50 years of age. Without timely and effective surgical intervention, natural disease progression leads to structural subchondral fracture, articular surface collapse, and secondary hip osteoarthritis, ultimately necessitating total hip arthroplasty (THA). Given the elevated lifetime revision rates of prosthetic replacements in young patients, joint-preserving strategies are prioritized during the precollapse window [primarily Association Research Circulation Osseous (ARCO) stages I, II, and early IIIA]. Vascularized bone grafting, specifically free vascularized fibular grafting (FVFG) and pedicled vascularized bone transfers, provides both living osteogenic scaffolding and direct arterial perfusion. Traditional manual techniques are limited by steep learning curves, prolonged fluoroscopy exposure, multiple off-target guide-wire passes, and variable spatial placement of the graft. Computer-assisted orthopedic surgical robots, real-time optoelectronic navigation, and multimodal 2D/3D registration can improve spatial accuracy, reduce the number of drilling attempts, and support more reproducible subchondral seating. This multidisciplinary expert consensus synthesizes available clinical series, meta-analyses, biomechanical evaluations, and multicenter experience to provide standardized recommendations on indications, preoperative planning, surgical technique, perioperative management, expected outcomes, and future directions for robot-assisted vascularized bone grafting in early ONFH. The document emphasizes workflows that may reduce fluoroscopy exposure, operative time, and technical variability while optimizing graft placement near the subchondral plate in the weight-bearing region. Consensus statements are graded according to the strength of supporting evidence (primarily retrospective cohorts and low- to moderate-quality meta-analyses) and expert agreement.

papers.title: Performance Analysis of Ensemble and Hybrid Deep Learning Models in Predicting Agricultural Chemical Residues and Crop Outcome
papers.abstract: The contemporary agricultural system has substantially transformed its productivity through extensive deployment of chemical pesticides, herbicides, and fertilizers. However, these practices introduce significant environmental sustainability concerns and human health risks. This paper conducts a comprehensive performance analysis of machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) techniques, with emphasis on ensemble and hybrid architectures, applied between 2018 and 2025 to investigate the relationship between agricultural chemical usage, crop yield outcomes, and human health consequences. Through systematic review of 26 peer-reviewed publications selected via PRISMA guidelines, this study evaluates convolutional neural networks (CNNs), long short-term memory (LSTM) networks, hybrid CNN-LSTM architectures, random forests, gradient boosting machines, and probabilistic models. Experimental findings demonstrate that CNN-LSTM hybrid models achieve R² > 0.93 for crop yield prediction, while Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) and Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) attain AUC scores up to 0.91 for health risk assessment. Multi-objective optimization frameworks combining NSGA-II with reinforcement learning yield Pareto-optimal chemical application strategies. Key challenges

papers.title: Predictive-feedforward energy management for a hybrid agricultural machine operating in mountainous orchards
papers.abstract: Hybrid agricultural machines in mountainous orchards operate under low-speed, high-load conditions with coupled gradient and time-varying rolling-resistance disturbances. Their power demand is therefore nonstationary and may change abruptly. Rule-based and instantaneous strategies provide limited preview, whereas model predictive control (MPC) can transmit prediction errors directly to actuator commands and imposes substantial online computation. To address these limitations, a forward model was developed for a power-split hybrid agricultural machine comprising an engine, two electric machines, a traction battery, and a planetary gear set. A predictive-feedforward, multi-objective energy-management strategy was proposed. Short-horizon speed and gradient predictions are normalized, weighted, and saturated to form a bounded load-risk indicator. Rather than entering low-level torque calculation directly, this indicator modifies the dynamic state-of-charge (SOC) safety boundary, power-source mode, and transmission-ratio switching threshold, thereby softly decoupling prediction and execution. Engine high-efficiency operation, two transmission ratios, and actuator constraints are then coordinated for computationally efficient online power allocation. With offline dynamic programming (DP) as a common benchmark, the strategy achieved 93.29–95.59% of the DP performance over cycles C1–C3, exceeding MPC by 1.41–3.19 percentage points and adaptive equivalent-consumption minimization by 3.62–4.99 percentage points. Mean execution time was 0.128–0.191 ms per step, 93.54% lower than that of MPC, while terminal SOC remained near 0.600. No SOC, battery-current, or power-source torque constraint was violated under prediction noise or abrupt equivalent rolling-resistance disturbances. The conclusions apply to maintained, firm orchard lanes with low track slip; soft-soil operation involving high traction, severe sinkage, or substantial slip requires further validation. Bounded load-risk feedforward thus retained short-horizon preview while limiting direct error propagation, providing a practical real-time approach for hybrid agricultural machines with resource-constrained embedded controllers.

papers.title: Physics-informed neural network for photoacoustic tomography reconstruction
papers.abstract: Abstract Objective: Conventional photoacoustic tomography (PAT) reconstruction algorithms often suffer from performance degradation under complex media and non-ideal detection conditions. To tackle these limitations, we propose a novel reconstruction method based on physics-informed neural networks (PINNs). Approach: The network model is optimized with constraints from observational data, wave equation, and initial conditions, to reconstruct the spatial distribution of initial acoustic pressure. The PINN framework further incorporates time reversal method to improve computational efficiency. Main results: Comprehensive PAT simulations demonstrate that the PINN achieves superior reconstruction quality compared with conventional algorithms. The PINN exhibits favorable adaptivity to both heterogeneous and lossy media, and strong robustness against noisy measurements, sparse sensor layouts and limited-view detection geometries. Significance: The PINN integrates the physical interpretability and the powerful capability of neural networks to represent continuous acoustic pressure fields. It eliminates the requirement for training datasets, offering broad application potential for PAT.

papers.title: AI-driven wear prediction for linear guides with physical constraints toward resilient manufacturing systems
papers.abstract: Monitoring the progressive degradation of linear guide systems under complex operating conditions is difficult using weak vibration signals, and existing data-driven methods generally suffer from insufficient integration of physical evolution laws and poor calibration of predictive uncertainty. This issue is particularly consequential in high-precision manufacturing, where unexpected wear-induced failures of linear guides can disrupt production continuity and undermine system resilience. To address these problems, this paper proposes an AI-driven wear prediction framework that integrates physical priors with adaptive physical constraints. First, coarse-grained physical prior features are extracted from wear profile data and concatenated with PCA-reduced vibration features to establish a dual-channel fusion mechanism. Second, a lightweight residual network enhances degradation feature extraction, while adaptive physical constraints dynamically balance prediction accuracy with physical regularity. Finally, within a pseudo-Bayesian physics-informed framework, a two-stage model selection and global variance scaling strategy is proposed to achieve well-calibrated uncertainty quantification under weak signal conditions. Experimental results on a linear guide degradation dataset show that the proposed method achieves an R² of 0.9553, MAE of 101.70 μm·mm, and RMSE of 143.26 μm·mm, with a 95% prediction interval coverage rate of 0.9460. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides reliable, uncertainty-aware wear-state prediction and RUL-oriented decision support for the predictive maintenance of linear guides. By enabling early degradation warning, informed maintenance planning, and rapid recovery preparation, the proposed method can contribute to reducing unplanned downtime and supporting the resilience of high-precision manufacturing systems.

papers.title: Geological Reliability in Deep Learning Mineral Prospectivity Mapping: A Review
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-based mineral prospectivity mapping (MPM) has rapidly advanced through the integration of deep learning, multisource geoscience data, and increasingly complex representation-learning approaches. However, the reliability of AI-derived prospectivity predictions remains a critical challenge because high predictive performance does not necessarily indicate geological validity, spatial transferability, or exploration usefulness. The key challenge is therefore not model complexity, but aligning geological knowledge, data representation, validation, and uncertainty assessment to ensure reliable interpretation. This review provides a structured critical synthesis of geological reliability in deep learning-based MPM, focusing on the methodological factors that influence whether AI outputs can support defensible exploration decisions. Rather than comparing algorithms solely by predictive accuracy, we examine the interconnected roles of geological representation, prediction support, label construction, negative-sample strategies, validation design, uncertainty quantification, explainability, transferability, and independent geological verification. Assessment of representative AI-based MPM studies reveals inconsistent reporting of these reliability dimensions, limiting reproducibility and meaningful comparison across studies. The review identifies recurring reliability bottlenecks, including spatial leakage caused by inappropriate validation strategies, uncertainty introduced during evidence-layer construction, ambiguity associated with unlabelled geological regions, and limitations in interpreting model explanations as geological causality. To organize these challenges, we propose a hierarchical evidence framework consisting of eight levels: methodological feasibility, internally validated predictive performance, spatial or temporal transferability, geological coherence, calibrated uncertainty, independent geological evidence, prospective field or drilling evidence, and demonstrated decision value. This framework clarifies the strength of claims that can be supported by different levels of evidence and provides a basis for transparent reporting and reliability assessment. Future progress in AI-based MPM will require integration of predictive capability with geological knowledge, robust validation, uncertainty-aware modelling, interpretable predictions, and independent geological verification. The proposed framework aims to support the development of more reproducible, transferable, and decision-relevant AI-assisted mineral exploration workflows.

papers.title: A machine learning framework for stage-structured predator–prey systems with fear effect: Sparse Identification, Gaussian Process Regression, and bifurcation analysis
papers.abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive machine learning framework for the analysis of a stage-structured predator–prey system incorporating the fear effect, intra-specific competition among juvenile predators, and maturation delay. The three-species model, comprising prey ( N ), juvenile predators ( P 1 ), and mature predators ( P 2 ), is governed by a non-linear ordinary differential equation system in which the prey growth rate is modulated by a fear factor 1/(1+ kP 2 ). We first establish the existence and local stability of the coexistence equilibrium E * = (16.02, 16.09, 32.19) and rigorously identify a supercritical Hopf bifurcation at a critical fear intensity k crit ≈ 0.067, beyond which the equilibrium becomes unstable and a stable limit cycle emerges. Five machine learning methods are deployed and benchmarked: (i) Sparse Identification of Non-linear Dynamics (SINDy) with a generic polynomial library, which recovers the predator equations exactly ( R 2 = 1.0) and approximates the prey equation ( R 2 = 0.9997); (ii) Dynamic Mode Decomposition (DMD), whose linear assumption yields poor reconstruction ( R 2 = −2.885 for P 2 ), demonstrating the inadequacy of linear methods for this non-linear system; (iii) Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) with a periodic–RBF composite kernel, achieving RMSE values of 1.92, 1.03, and 0.84 from sparse noisy observations; (iv) a physics-constrained function approximation for recovering population trajectories from incomplete data; and (v) a polynomial surrogate ODE model for derivative field approximation. Additionally, the effect of maturation delay τ on system stability is examined through delay differential equation analysis with a fourth-order Runge–Kutta integrator, revealing delay-induced destabilization and transitions to limit cycle dynamics at τ ≥ 10. All numerical results are independently verified and all performance metrics are computed from actual analyses. The framework provides a rigorous, reproducible methodology for applying modern data-driven methods to stage-structured ecological models.

papers.title: Nonlinear Model Predictive Control of an Automotive PEMFC System Considering Anode Recirculation Loop Bleeding
papers.abstract: This work presents a Nonlinear Model Predictive Controller (NMPC) strategy for the optimal operation of a fuel cell system to maximize its average efficiency and minimize degradation. Because of the different time scales associated with the different controlled variables, the proposed NMPC is divided into three distinct parts, each one customized with its specific prediction horizon and sampling time. The NMPC is based on a comprehensive model of the fuel cell stack, considering manufacturing constraints and incorporating the compressor map. The NMPC outputs are the optimal setpoints for all the subsystems’ local controllers. The studied fuel cell system incorporates the anode recirculation loop with an ejector, a water separator, and a bleed valve, and the proposed NMPC determines the optimal opening percentage of the bleed valve to prevent nitrogen accumulation and efficiency distortion. The proposed strategy yields higher efficiency than offline steady-state setpoints in the evaluated scenario, while full future-current information generally provides further improvement relative to limited preview.

papers.title: Toward integrated multimodal artificial intelligence in bone marrow examination: current state and open challenges
papers.abstract: Bone marrow (BM) examinations are intrinsically multimodal: hematopathologists integrate peripheral blood, aspirate cytomorphology, trephine histology, flow cytometry, cytogenetics, and molecular genetics data into a single interpretation. Because WHO-HAEM5 and ICC 2022 define entities through integrated morphological, immunophenotypic, cytogenetic, and molecular criteria, multimodal diagnostic reasoning embedded in a procedural workflow, not isolated image classification, represents the appropriate target for the use of artificial intelligence (AI). We review the existing research on integrated multimodal AI systems for BM examination by classifying these systems into three categories: mature single-modality tools; systems that perform cross-modal prediction, in which one modality is estimated from another; and genuine multimodal fusion systems, in which several modalities are jointly ingested by a single model. Evidence is stronger at the single-modality level, where deep learning approaches expert performance in aspirate cytology, trephine histology, and flow cytometry assessments, and the first Food and Drug Administration (FDA) De Novo–authorized all-digital bone marrow aspirate (BMA) application has defined a new device category. On the other hand, while cross-modal prediction is rapidly expanding, genuine multimodal fused systems that jointly ingest matched morphology, flow, molecular, and clinical data to yield unified guideline-aligned recommendations remain unrealized. Direct head-to-head evidence is sparse and endpoint-dependent; nevertheless, the lack of demonstrated superiority over the strongest single-modality comparator does not automatically imply the absence of benefits. The dominant obstacles are fusion of heterogeneous modalities with missing data, absence of large paired multi-institutional datasets and harmonized nomenclature, class imbalances, batch-effect-driven generalization failures, immature explainability, uncertainty quantification, and regulatory pathways. Nevertheless, integrated multimodal AI systems for BM examinations have entered a promising early translational phase, and the field should aim to pursue integration using paired datasets, explicit fusion architectures, calibrated abstention-aware models, and staged prospective validation.

papers.title: Coordinated ramp metering under asymmetric traffic demand: a continuous deep reinforcement learning approach
papers.abstract: Asymmetric ramp demand is common in multi-ramp freeway corridors and can complicate coordinated ramp metering. Existing approaches may not explicitly represent differences in short-term queue growth across ramps, while discrete metering actions can limit control resolution. This study proposes a soft actor–critic-based coordinated ramp-metering framework in which the control problem is formulated as a continuous-action Markov decision process. A queue-growth asymmetry index is incorporated into the state representation to characterise uneven queue development, and continuous green times are assigned jointly to the controlled ramps. The framework is evaluated under symmetric, static asymmetric and dynamic asymmetric demand scenarios. Comparisons with no control, heuristic ramp-metering coordination and model predictive control are conducted using five independent random seeds. Relative to no control, the maximum travel-time reduction and speed improvement are 31.36% and 64.91%, respectively, while the maximum ramp queues remain below the overflow threshold. Ablation results show that removing the queue-growth asymmetry index or replacing continuous actions with discrete green-time levels reduces traffic performance. Reward-component ablations further indicate that the overflow penalty mainly limits ramp queue accumulation, whereas the occupancy-gradient penalty contributes more to mainline speed. These results indicate that the proposed framework provides effective coordinated control under the tested demand conditions.
