papers.title: Digital Intelligence-Enabled Value-Infused Teaching in Public Finance: A Four-Dimensional Framework for Curriculum Ideological and Political Education
papers.abstract: Digitalisation is opening up new avenues for connecting disciplinary learning with value education in higher education. Digital tools have not automatically resolved the division between fiscal knowledge and questions of public interest, social equity and government responsibility in public finance. Based on relevant literature and three years of teaching public finance to second-year undergraduates, this study has identified four practical problems: the lack of integration between fiscal knowledge and public values; insufficient opportunities for contextualised and active learning; a scarcity of teaching cases; and difficulties in evaluating value-oriented learning. Therefore, it has put forward a four-dimensional system of content integration, teaching implementation, resource support and evaluation and feedback. A resource-constrained ecological infrastructure investment scenario in a hypothetical area of the upper Yellow River Basin is used to illustrate the framework.The scenario provides public policy materials and simulates funding constraints, allowing students to prioritise projects, make financing decisions, consider provision arrangements, and evaluate the cost-effectiveness of expenditure. It has not been officially introduced at this time and therefore cannot be presented as a result of a controlled experiment. Although the digital platform can be employed to organise preparation, communication, resources and process documentation, teachers’ professional judgement is still required for the interpretation of students’ reasoning and values.

papers.abstract: В статье проводится анализ применения методов машинного обучения для повышения вычислительной эффективности задач вычислительной гидродинамики (CFD). Рассмотрены ключевые направления интеграции машинного обучения в моделирование течений: суррогатное моделирование, разработка условий притока для турбулентности, оптимизация аэродинамических форм и неразрушающее зондирование полей течения. Особое внимание уделено физически информированным нейронным сетям (PINN — Physics-Informed Neural Network) и гибридным архитектурам, позволяющим соблюдать законы сохранения. Показано, что, несмотря на значительное сокращение времени расчетов, применение «чистых» моделей машинного обучения сталкивается с проблемами сходимости при наличии высокочастотных особенностей и трудностями обеспечения физической согласованности (несжимаемость, сохранение импульса). Сформулированы рекомендации по балансировке градиентов и выбору архитектур для решения жестких задач оптимизации. Работа представляет интерес для разработчиков CFD-кодов и специалистов в области аэродинамики и гидродинамики.

papers.title: Machine Learning & Artificial Intelligence in the Development of Gastro-Retentive Drug Delivery Systems: Current Advances & Future Prospectives
papers.abstract: The integration of machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence (AI) into pharmaceutical sciences is reshaping the development of advanced drug delivery systems. Traditional gastroprotective drug delivery systems (GRDDS) are designed to prolong the residence time of oral dosage forms in the stomach to enhance bioavailability and therapeutic efficacy for drugs with narrow absorption windows. However, conventional formulation development often relies on empirical optimization, which is time-consuming and resource-intensive. AI and ML bring a data-driven paradigm to this complex landscape by enabling computational modeling, predictive analytics, and intelligent optimization of formulation parameters. These technologies can analyze multidimensional datasets to identify patterns and relationships between formulation components, physiological variables, and release kinetics that would be challenging to discern using traditional methods. AI-assisted models such as artificial neural networks, support vector machines, and Bayesian optimization have demonstrated significant potential in predicting drug release profiles, selecting optimal polymer systems, and simulating gastric behavior. Moreover, AI can streamline experimental design, reduce trial-anderror iterations, and accelerate the development timeline, thus improving formulation robustness and performance. The convergence of AI with gastroprotective systems also promises personalized approaches that account for patient-specific gastric motility and physiological factors, fostering tailored therapies. Although challenges remain—such as the need for high-quality datasets, interpretability of complex models, and integration with regulatory frameworks—the current advances provide a compelling foundation for future research. Embracing these intelligent tools in GRDDS development is likely to expand the frontiers of oral drug delivery by enhancing design precision, improving therapeutic outcomes, and reducing developmental costs. Continued innovation and interdisciplinary collaboration will be essential to fully harness the transformative potential of AI and ML in pharmaceutics.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Driven Optimization of Multiphase Chemical Processes for Energy-Efficient and Sustainable Manufacturing
papers.abstract: There are many industrial chemical manufacturing processes that involve multi-phase chemistry, such as gas–liquid, liquid–liquid, gas–solid, solid–liquid and three-phase systems, and these are among the most energy-intensive and complex unit processes to optimise, due to the complex, nonlinear and often unmeasurable interfacial phenomena. The hydrodynamic, thermal and mass transfer coupling involved in these systems are difficult to model with traditional first-principles or empirical optimization approaches and make it challenging to progress towards industrially relevant scales and energy efficient, sustainable manufacturing targets. This narrative review aims to collect and condense the surge of literature on the application of machine learning (ML) algorithms for optimizing multiphase chemical processes, which spans from classic statistical process control (SPC) to advanced data-driven, hybrid and physics-informed learning algorithms. We study the use of supervised learning, deep learning, reinforcement learning, Bayesian optimization and evolutionary algorithms in important multiphase unit operations for surrogate modelling, soft sensing, real-time control and multi-objective optimization. The literature reviewed indicates that the combined results of the different strategies with ML can produce energy efficiency gains ranging from 8% - 28%, improvements in yield and product quality and predictive accuracy can be identified, and computational costs can be reduced when compared to other conventional approaches such as computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and first-principles (FP). The challenges highlighted include issues such as limited data, interpretability of models, scalability, and real-time deployment. The future scope for this research is physics-informed and hybrid models, digital twins, transfer and federated learning, and benchmarking.

papers.title: Wave as Disturbance and Signal in a Physics-Informed Framework for Shallow Water Bathymetry
papers.abstract: Satellite-derived bathymetry (SDB) commonly treats the sea surface as a source of radiometric disturbance, although the same surface wave field can also contain water depth information through gravity wave propagation. This article presents a Wave-Aware Physics-Informed Neural Network (WA-PINN) that represents these two roles within a unified shallow water bathymetry framework. The optical geometry stream combines Sentinel-2 multispectral observations with seafloor geometry. The disturbance stream converts European Centre for Medium Range Weather Forecasts Reanalysis Version 5 (ERA5) wind forcing into Mean Square Slope (MSS) through the Cox–Munk relationship and introduces a roughness-dependent sunglint contribution into the optical physics constraint. The signal stream retrieves local wavelength, propagation direction, and wave celerity from Sentinel-2 surface texture and constrains predicted depth with the finite depth gravity wave dispersion relation. A Wave Validity Factor (WVF) controls the influence of the dispersion constraint according to the coherence and physical plausibility of the retrieved wave field. The three streams are fused in a shared depth predictor constrained by supervised depth loss, optical physics loss, and wave dispersion physics loss. The framework is demonstrated over Culebra, St. Thomas, and St. John in the northeastern Caribbean Sea. The complete Dual Role model reaches an overall Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 1.21 m, a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) 0.77 m, and an R2 of 0.96. Relative to the Slope Aware configuration, the Disturbance and Signal models reduce RMSE by 15.7% and 12.8%, while the complete model reduces RMSE by 29.7%. The disturbance contribution increases under stronger wind forcing, whereas the signal contribution increases with WVF. Depth-dependent RMSE increases from 0.82 m at 0 to 5 m to 1.58 m at 20 to 30 m. These results illustrate the intended complementarity between correcting wave-induced optical contamination and exploiting wave propagation as an additional depth constraint.

papers.title: Multivariable control of large-scale pressurized water reactor based on LPV-MPC algorithm over a wide operating range
papers.abstract: For energy conservation, large-scale Pressurized Water Reactors (PWRs) are required to participate in grid peak shaving. Compared to traditional PID control, Model Predictive Control (MPC) algorithm offers advantages in handling multivariable control problems. However, PWR systems exhibit strong nonlinearity under wide-range operation, limiting conventional MPC performance. Therefore, Linear Parameter Varying (LPV) models, valued for their nonlinear approximation capability and low computational cost, are employed in nonlinear MPC. This paper proposes an LPV model-based MPC algorithm to enhance the control of a nonlinear HPR1000 model. An iterative optimization strategy is adopted for LPV model identification: first, initial local models are identified using the asymptotic method; then, parameters of the weighting functions are estimated via least squares; finally, the LPV model is optimized iteratively based on the total data. The local models demonstrate good performance in both time-domain and frequency-domain validation. The optimized LPV model shows high similarity to the plant’s step responses at both high and low loads, confirming its suitability for MPC controller. The LPV-MPC is compared with both the original control system and a fixed-model MPC (F-MPC) through test scenarios at 100 % and 50 % FP. The results indicate that the LPV-MPC controller offers comparable performance at 100 % FP, but exhibits faster regulation speed and stronger capability in suppressing SG water level fluctuations at 50 % FP. The comparison with F-MPC demonstrates that the LPV-MPC possesses stronger adaptability and robustness. Meanwhile, a large-scale transition scenario was implemented. The comparative analysis confirms that the LPV-MPC controller possesses superior load-following performance.

papers.title: Multi-Level Text Alignment for Interpretable and Uncertainty-Aware Time Series Forecasting with LLMs
papers.abstract: Adapting large language models (LLMs) for time series forecasting introduces unique challenges due to the mismatch between continuous time series tokens and the discrete word tokens LLMs are trained on. While LLMs have shown success on natural language tasks, aligning time series tokens with the semantic space of LLMs while preserving both accuracy and interpretability remains an open problem. Existing reprogramming and prompt-based approaches often generate word embeddings that are misaligned with or semantically irrelevant to the corresponding time series. For example, a segment with an increasing trend may be mapped to words like ”mirror” or ”keyboard”, which makes them hard to interpret. To bridge the gap, we propose MLTA-LLM, a Multi-Level Text Alignment framework for time series forecasting with LLMs. MLTA-LLM decomposes time series into trend, seasonal, and residual components, each of which is aligned with semantic anchor embeddings or text prototype embeddings. This component-specific alignment forces the LLM to process time series data through structured, interpretable representations. In addition, we integrate conformal prediction to provide statistically rigorous prediction intervals for uncertainty quantification. Experiments on multiple benchmark datasets show that MLTA-LLM not only improves forecasting accuracy over state-of-the-art baselines but also yields more interpretable representations and better-calibrated uncertainty estimates.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Bioengineering: Innovations, Challenges, and Future Directions: A Narrative Review
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming bioengineering, with applications ranging from diagnosis and biomedical imaging to wearable technologies, rehabilitation, biomaterials, biofabrication, and digital twins. This narrative review aims to examine the major innovations, challenges, and future directions of AI-enabled bioengineering, with particular attention to its clinical and translational development. The literature was searched in Scopus and PubMed, with emphasis on systematic reviews and meta-analyses and consideration of other relevant secondary literature across the main bioengineering domains. A total of 57 secondary publications were included in the principal evidence base. The review process was additionally informed by the ANDJ Narrative Review Checklist and an established qualification and scoring methodology applied to the selected secondary literature. The reviewed evidence shows a broad expansion of AI applications and increasing integration of intelligent technologies into bioengineering systems. However, important challenges remain, particularly regarding data quality and representativeness, validation and generalizability, reproducibility, safety, human oversight, ethical responsibility, equity, and regulatory requirements. Future developments are expected to increasingly involve multimodal, adaptive, connected, and human-centered systems integrating AI with sensing technologies, robotics, digital twins, and longitudinal data. Overall, AI-enabled bioengineering is progressing from promising technological applications toward increasingly integrated and translational systems. Its successful evolution will depend on combining technological innovation with robust clinical evidence, responsible development, and appropriate ethical and regulatory frameworks.

papers.title: Bayesian Inverse Optimisation under Uncertainty Posterior Inference for Hidden Decision Objectives
papers.abstract: Inverse optimization seeks the hidden objective that explains observed decisions, yet existing methods typically recover a single objective and ignore uncertainty in the underlying preferences. We develop a Bayesian framework that represents the unknown objective by a posterior distribution, combining a boundedrationality choice model with prior information to quantify uncertainty directly. We establish geometric conditions for identifiability, prove posterior consistency, derive the optimal n−1/2, contraction rate, obtain a Bernstein–von Mises approximation, and present a finite-sample concentration bound together with a robust fractional posterior for misspecified behavioural models. Posterior inference is performed using gradient-based Markov chain Monte Carlo and a Laplace approximation. Simulation studies demonstrate accurate recovery under noisy, misspecified, nonlinear, and high-dimensional settings, while a controlled clinical example illustrates uncertainty quantification in hidden decision preferences. The proposed framework extends inverse optimization from point estimation to statistically principled uncertainty quantification, providing a rigorous foundation for learning decision objectives from imperfect observations.

papers.title: Estimation of aggregate flexibility regions for distributed flexible resources using limited information
papers.abstract: Distributed flexible resources (DFRs) can support power-system operation only if aggregators can report their flexibility regions as operating conditions change. Existing aggregation methods generally require detailed device-level states, which may be unavailable, as well as repeated online optimization. This paper proposes a limited-information physics-informed neural network (PINN) for estimating aggregate flexibility regions of DFRs. Its inputs are low-dimensional operating-condition descriptors, and its output is a feasibility-oriented representative polyhedral region conditioned on those descriptors. Physical feasibility and boundary tightness are embedded through support- and projection-based errors and differentiable active-hyperplane residuals, enabling training without precomputed ground-truth flexibility-region labels. The proposed pretraining, full-network training, and loss-weight scheduling scheme prioritizes physical feasibility while retaining boundary tightness. Case studies show that the estimated regions vary predictably with operating conditions and achieve a favorable balance between physical implementability and economic performance relative to alternative aggregation models. Across the operational tests, 96.25% of PINN dispatch trajectories had zero relative disaggregation error, and the maximum error was 4.72%. Dispatch costs remained comparable to those of the full-information inner approximation. Once trained, the estimator requires neither complete device-level information nor an online optimization solver. The proposed framework therefore lowers the deployment barrier for condition-dependent flexibility estimation in practical distributed-resource aggregation.

papers.title: Size and geometry effects on the flow-rate–torque trade-off of a drainage impeller in a submerged mechanical defoamer
papers.abstract: Abstract Rotating drainage impellers must balance suction-driven flow against shaft loading, yet which geometric parameters govern this flow-rate–torque trade-off remains poorly established. This work addresses this question for the drainage impeller of a submerged mechanical defoamer, focusing on the single-phase hydrodynamics underlying froth capture rather than directly modelling foam rupture. Thirty configurations spanning four geometric parameters — blade number Z, impeller diameter D, impeller height H and blade outlet angle β — were generated by maximin orthogonal Latin hypercube sampling and evaluated by three-dimensional steady-state CFD for drainage flow rate and torque. Gaussian-process surrogates with leave-one-out cross-validation then supported conditional-response analysis, Sobol sensitivity indices and surrogate-based multi-objective Bayesian optimization. The results show that impeller diameter dominates the dimensional responses, with first-order Sobol indices of 0.91 for flow rate and 0.96 for torque. After dimensional normalization removes the leading size-scaling effects, diameter still governs the flow coefficient, whereas impeller height emerges as the principal secondary factor for the torque coefficient, indicating that size mainly sets the operating point while the residual geometry modulates the normalized loading. A representative Pareto compromise design (Z = 8, D = 81.11 mm, H = 30 mm, β = 120°) was verified by CFD within 6% of the surrogate predictions; relative to the original impeller it raises the flow rate by 25.5%, a gain attributable mainly to the enlarged diameter rather than to improve dimensionless flow capacity. Water experiments at 1000 rev/min confirmed the CFD predictions for both impellers, with flow-rate deviations within 5% and torque deviations within 10%. Flow-field analysis relates the higher throughput to an enlarged suction-related low-pressure region, smoother blade-passage flow and reduced local wake dissipation. The framework provides a practical basis for drainage-impeller design and, more generally, for separating size and geometry effects in CFD-based optimization under limited simulation budgets.

papers.title: Bayesian optimization-driven machine learning for compressive strength prediction of hybrid fiber-reinforced recycled aggregate concrete
papers.abstract: The use of recycled coarse aggregate (RCA) in concrete provides a sustainable approach to reducing construction and demolition waste, but predicting its compressive strength (CS) is challenging due to complex interactions among binder composition, supplementary cementitious materials (SCMs), fibers, and mix proportions. This study develops and compares seven Bayesian optimization (BO) based machine learning (ML) models to predict the CS of hybrid fiber-reinforced recycled aggregate concrete (HFRRAC). A dataset of 281 experimental samples with 14 input variables, including OPC, FA, GGBS, water content, aggregate proportions, and fiber characteristics, was used for model training and evaluation. Performance was assessed using R 2 , RMSE, MAE, and MAPE. The results show that ensemble and boosting methods outperform the conventional approaches evaluated in this study. On the held-out testing subset, the best-performing BO-GP-GBQR model achieved a training R 2 of 0.9959 and a testing R 2 of 0.9348, with a testing RMSE of 3.5675 MPa, MAE of 2.4883 MPa, and MAPE of 8.03%. SHAP analysis identified water content, OPC, and GGBS as the most influential parameters. The proposed framework enables accurate and interpretable prediction of 28-day CS and can support preliminary mixture screening for HFRRAC containing recycled coarse aggregate and hybrid fibers.

papers.title: AI-Guided Clinical Image Interpretation System for Precision Treatment Planning
papers.abstract: Radiological examinations increasingly leverage artificial intelligence to enhance diagnostic performance by compensating for expertise shortages, particularly in specialized interpretation. Despite academic AI models achieving compelling accuracy, adoption remains low. An objective, evidence-based examination of AI-guided clinical image interpretation seeks to expose the underlying reasons. The primary challenge lies not in accuracy but in fully automated analysis, especially for multimodal and multidimensional datasets. Introduction of uncertainty measures, image explainability, and real-world data reduce recognition to a decisive-supporting role—helping radiologists to detect previously unnoticed abnormalities—or even to precautionary analysis. Patients requesting precision medicine and therapy planning—and those at high risk of neglected pathology—stand to gain the greatest benefit. Relevant AI architecture considers imaging cues suitable for precision medicine or requiring additional methods to obtain interpretable images. Successful performance testing against an external, hidden reference dataset promotes vital user trust. Machine learning achieves best results where all potentially pathological abnormalities are identified and their presence virtually guaranteed, as in multi-class recognition. Data scarcity, however, impedes clinically relevant solutions. Explainability, essential for medical applications and clinical acceptance, extends simply beyond clinical decision support to provide saliency maps and, better still, clinically meaningful image regions or qualities. Attention maps may even bring a form of rule-based reasoning within reach. Clinical integration that reproduces the technical conditions under which model diagnostic measures are calculated raises the challenge of uncertainty quantification—a necessary condition for clinical decision support. Convolutional neural networks trained for photo-quality classification, par excellence supervised image quality assessment, provide the basic cues for uncertainty quantification. Imaging acquisition, modality, and systems are also defined in terms of current PACS/EPIC systems. PE, pre-symptomatic examination or precautionary examination, is defined as a patient-user group prepared to cover the cost of an examination with lower diagnostic accuracy and a high level of uncertainty.

papers.title: A structure-preserving potential-Logphi framework for forward approximation and coefficient identification of extended CBS-like nonlinear wave equations
papers.abstract: Abstract The extended Calogero--Bogoyavlenskii--Schiff-like equation is a representative $(2+1)$-dimensional nonlinear evolution equation in mathematical physics. For coupled formulations of such nonlinear systems, conventional multi-output physics-informed neural networks may not explicitly preserve intrinsic compatibility relations between physical fields. In this work, a structure-preserving Potential-Logphi PINN is developed for the forward approximation and inverse coefficient identification of the extended CBS-like equation. In the proposed framework, the neural network represents a scalar potential $v_\theta(x,y,t)$, from which the coupled fields are reconstructed by automatic differentiation as $u_\theta=\partial_x v_\theta$ and $w_\theta=\partial_y v_\theta$. This potential representation naturally satisfies the compatibility relation $u_y-w_x=0$. Five exact-solution benchmarks with lump, soliton, periodic, and mixed interaction structures are investigated. Numerical results show that the proposed framework accurately reconstructs complex localized wave fields and provides stable derivative information for coefficient identification. Across three independent runs in the matched comparison, the proposed Potential-Logphi formulation achieves the lowest mean relative-$L_2$ errors for both coupled fields among all five evaluated model formulations. The Potential-Logphi formulation therefore provides a structure-consistent neural approach for learning coupled nonlinear wave equations with tau-function-based solution structures.

papers.title: Deep-Learning Error Correction of Regional Significant Wave Height Forecasts
papers.abstract: Deep-learning post-processing can correct systematic errors in numerical wave forecasts, but its reliability under high-wave conditions remains unclear. We develop an error-correction framework in which deep networks predict the full future error trajectory of operational forecasts, and compare three architectures, a pure LSTM, a pure Transformer and a hybrid LSTM–Transformer, tuned identically with Bayesian optimization, using hourly observations from six buoys in the Bohai Sea and Yellow Sea over 2023–2025. On the full test sample all models improve the 72 h forecasts by 15.37% to 23.93% in RMSE, with the hybrid model attaining the lowest pooled RMSE; on the high-wave subset with SWH above 1.5 m, however, all three degrade the forecast, increasing RMSE by 7.58% to 9.05%. An exact decomposition of the squared-error change shows that fluctuation-capturing skill remains intact while the degradation is driven by the mean term: trained on samples dominated by low and moderate waves, the correctors learn a globally averaged adjustment whose sign opposes the reversed raw bias at high waves. Neither loss reweighting nor filtered training resolves this degradation at the 72 h horizon. Shortening the horizon to 24 h restores positive skill, with RMSE reductions of 4.43% to 7.88%, and reverses the ranking in favor of the pure LSTM. These findings indicate that architecture rankings are horizon-dependent, and they are consistent with the interpretation that extreme-condition skill is limited by the information content of the predictors rather than by model capacity.

papers.title: Hierarchical RL–ANFIS Energy Management with Supervisory Override for Priority-Aware Microgrids Under Measured Iraqi Grid Outages
papers.abstract: Grid-deficient environments such as Iraq experience frequent and prolonged outages, forcing buildings to operate as isolated microgrids for substantial periods. This study proposes a hierarchical hybrid energy management controller combining a tabular Q-learning supervisory master based on reinforcement learning (RL), an Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS) tactical slave, and a physical safety layer that protects urgent-load service whenever physically feasible. The controller was evaluated over a full year using measured Iraqi irradiance and grid-availability data and compared with rule-based, standalone ANFIS, standalone RL, model predictive control, and perfect-foresight dynamic programming benchmarks. For the learned controllers, annual performance is reported as mean ± standard deviation across four independent retraining runs, while generalisation is assessed separately using a seasonally distributed four-month temporal hold-out. The Hybrid achieved a mean annual cost of $9353.49 ± 122.63, a 20.91% reduction relative to the deterministic rule-based baseline. It also reduced diesel use by 55.6%, generator starts by 56.4%, and deep-discharge events by 54.8%, while maintaining 100% urgent-load service. Standalone RL used less fuel but showed more generator cycling and deep discharge. On the 11,808-timestep hold-out, normalised cost differed by 2.6% for RL and 1.2% for ANFIS between training and test periods. The Hybrid mean annual cost was 12.48% above the perfect-foresight DP lower bound. These results support the proposed architecture as a lightweight, priority-aware option for weak-grid microgrids.

papers.title: AI-guided extraction of plant-derived bioactives for edible packaging films
papers.abstract: The increasing concern for plastic pollution and the rising demand for sustainable food packaging, have accelerated research on edible packaging films fortified with bioactive compounds from plants. Phytochemicals such as flavonoids, terpenoids and polyphenols confer antioxidant, antimicrobial and functional properties to improve food safety, maintain quality and extend shelf-life. However, conventional extraction methods such as Soxhlet, maceration and solvent extraction have disadvantages of high solvent and energy consumption, low selectivity and extraction efficiency and thermal degradation of bioactives. Furthermore, the nonlinear relationships among the extraction variables are complex and limit the performance of conventional statistical optimization methods. This review critically examines the integration of conventional statistical optimization tools, especially response surface methodology (RSM) and design of experiments (DoE), with machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) strategies for advanced green extraction processes such as microwave-assisted, ultrasound-assisted, enzyme-assisted, supercritical fluid, pulsed electric field, and pressurized liquid extraction. RSM/DoE helps in systematic experimental design and optimization of processes, whereas ML methods, including Artificial Neural Network (ANN), Support Vector Regression (SVR), Random Forest (RF), and Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS), enable data-assisted prediction of nonlinear relationships. DL architectures, including Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), autoencoders (AE), transformers, and Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs), support complex and high-dimensional datasets when sufficient training data are available; However, their significance in edible packaging research, where datasets are relatively small and heterogeneous, must be addressed in terms of model complexity, overfitting and validation robustness. It further evaluates AI-guided incorporation of plant bioactives into edible packaging through optimized encapsulation, prediction of mechanical and barrier properties, controlled release behavior, safety assessment, and sustainability evaluation. AI-assisted and hybrid models have demonstrated, in various reported studies, enhanced predictive accuracy and optimization efficacy compared with conventional response surface methodology in terms of extraction yield, solvent use, energy demand and experimental trials. However, the limitations of standardised datasets, computational complexity, regulatory issues and lack of large-scale validation restrict the applications in industry. The reviewed literature still provides limited evidence directly linking mechanical, barrier and release properties, as well as safety outcomes such as migration, to ML-based modeling and optimization. Formulation-specific experimental validation is therefore still required. Future advances in explainable AI frameworks, harmonized databases, industrial-scale studies and multidisciplinary collaboration will be crucial for the commercialization of intelligent and sustainable edible packaging systems. Further scale-up studies are needed before these approaches can be considered viable for industrial application. Their translation will depend on process reproducibility, regulatory acceptance, sufficiently large and representative datasets, appropriate computational resources, formulation-specific testing, mechanism-informed modeling and uncertainty quantification. Any proposed formulation will also require independent experimental validation, together with food-safety and shelf-life studies, before it can be accepted for food-contact applications.

papers.title: AI-driven analysis of bioconvective Casson–Williamson penta-hybrid nanofluid flow over exponentially stretching surface using ANN and physics-informed neural networks
papers.abstract: Purpose This study aims to explore the bioconvective flow of a Casson–Williamson penta-hybrid nanofluid across an exponentially stretching permeable surface. The analysis accounts for the joint effects of a magnetic field, porous medium, thermal radiation, Brownian motion, thermophoresis, heat generation and chemical reaction on the transport behavior. Design/methodology/approach The physical problem is described through the governing partial differential equations for momentum, energy, concentration and the movement of motile microorganisms. Suitable similarity transformations reduce these dimensional equations into a coupled set of nonlinear ordinary differential equations, which are then solved numerically using the bvp4c technique in MATLAB. To complement the numerical work, an artificial neural network based on the Levenberg–Marquardt Algorithm (ANN-LMA) and a physics-informed NN (PINN) framework are constructed to predict the Nusselt number across mono-hybrid, tri-hybrid, tetra-hybrid and penta-hybrid nanoparticle systems. Findings The results reveal that increasing the magnetic field, porosity, Casson and Williamson parameters slows the fluid motion, while thermal radiation, Brownian motion, thermophoresis and heat generation raise the temperature within the boundary layer. The density of motile microorganisms falls as the Lewis and Peclet numbers grow. A comparative assessment shows that the penta-hybrid nanofluid outperforms the mono-hybrid, tri-hybrid and tetra-hybrid systems in heat transfer, mass transport and microorganism flux, a consequence of the stronger interaction among the dispersed nanoparticles. Originality/value Both the ANN-LMA and PINN models achieve very low mean squared error values and align closely with the numerical solutions, capturing the heat transfer response with notable precision. This work highlights the practical importance of penta-hybrid nanofluids and neural-network-based prediction tools for advanced thermal engineering and bioconvective transport applications. The ANN-LMA and PINN models achieved correlation coefficients close to unity (R≈1) and MSEs of the order of 10−10, confirming excellent predictive accuracy.

papers.title: Data-Driven Modeling of Ship Maneuvering Dynamics via Control-Aware Hankel-DMDc and Mode Attribution
papers.abstract: Accurate data-driven identification and long-term forecasting of surface ship motions in realistic ocean environments are essential for advanced autonomous navigation and predictive control systems. However, robust system identification in such conditions remains challenging due to high-frequency wave-induced disturbances, which contaminate measured signals and may contribute to error accumulation in recursive forecasting. This paper proposes a control- and wave-aware data-driven framework for modeling and prediction of ship maneuvering dynamics in stochastic wave environments. The approach integrates Hankel dynamic mode decomposition with control (Hankel-DMDc) with a spectral Mode Attribution Layer that characterizes modal associations with commanded control inputs and measured wave excitation. A dual-criterion selection rule, based on the Wave Energy Projection (WEP) and Control Correlation Index (CCI), is introduced to characterize and separate maneuvering-related and wave-associated modal content without relying on a predefined physical model. The framework is evaluated on a multidimensional ship-motion dataset from the DaRUS repository, using routine maneuvering trajectories for model identification and independent out-of-distribution test trajectories for prediction evaluation. One-step prediction analysis indicates high local accuracy, particularly for rotational states, while recursive multi-step forecasting shows gradual error growth over a 200-step prediction horizon. A quantitative comparison with unfiltered Hankel-DMDc, conventional Butterworth filtering, and direct wave-input modeling further shows that the proposed framework retains predictive performance comparable to direct Hankel-DMDc for the present dataset, while providing explicit modal attribution and wave/maneuvering characterization. The identified discrete-time operator also exhibits a spectral radius below unity, while no rapid divergence is observed over the evaluated recursive prediction horizon. The proposed methodology provides an interpretable data-driven framework for modeling marine systems, with potential applicability to control-oriented system identification, predictive modeling, autonomous navigation, and Model Predictive Control (MPC).

papers.title: Investigation of surface topography and potential thrombogenic implications of SLM 3D-printed SS316L cardiovascular stent using hybrid post-processing
papers.abstract: This investigation focuses on a 3D-printed SS316L stent fabricated using Selective Laser Melting (SLM) to improve surface quality through post-processing. Four conditions were investigated: heat-treatment followed by electropolishing (HT-EP), electropolishing only (EP), heat-treatment only (HT), and without heat-treatment or electropolishing, i.e., as-built (W-HT-EP). Surface roughness was evaluated using Ra, Rq, Rz, Rt, skewness (Rsk), and kurtosis (Rku) using three independently fabricated stents per condition (n = 3). The HT-EP condition exhibited the lowest roughness, with Ra = 0.498 ± 0.014 µm, Rq = 0.546 ± 0.077 µm, Rz = 2.053 ± 0.228 µm, and Rt = 2.630 ± 0.186 µm. The corresponding Rsk and Rku values were 0.664 ± 0.061 and 2.346 ± 0.110, respectively. The Ra value of HT-EP represented an 81% reduction compared with W-HT-EP and a 38.5% reduction compared with EP alone. One-way ANOVA showed statistically significant differences (p ≤ .001), with HT-EP Tukey’s HSD analysis (p < .001). SEM revealed a uniform and defect-free morphology. HT-EP provided favorable characteristics and potential to reduce surface-topography-derived Thrombogenicity Risk Index (TRI).

papers.title: Machine Learning Modeling of Drill Cuttings Transport Based on Computational Fluid Dynamics Simulation Data
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Drill cuttings transport is a critical operation in drilling deep wells. Inefficient removal of cuttings can lead to both hydraulic and mechanical problems during drilling operations. High‐fidelity computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations provide detailed insight but are computationally expensive. Alternative models often oversimplify the relationships between operational parameters and particle transport, thereby failing to predict critical quantities. These quantities include transport efficiency or cuttings concentrations. In this study, surrogate models are developed using a common data set generated by validated multiphase CFD simulations. The data set consists of 269 CFD simulations varying the Reynolds number, Taylor number, particle concentration, and particle size. Five surrogate models, namely, Decision Trees (DTs), Random Forest (RF), Extra Trees (XTRs), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and Gaussian process regression (GPR), were trained to predict the domain‐averaged particle velocity. The models are evaluated in terms of prediction accuracy, learning behavior with respect to training data size, robustness through bootstrap resampling, and physical consistency of the response trends. All trained models achieved very high predictive accuracy (), confirming that CFD‐based particle transport can be reliably emulated using data‐driven surrogates. The learning‐curve analysis showed that performance improves rapidly with increasing data, saturating beyond approximately 60% of the data set. Despite the statistical accuracy, tree‐based ensembles produced piecewise‐constant, nonsmooth response surfaces. However, GPR generated smoother and more physically consistent trends. Sensitivity analysis revealed that the Reynolds number dominates the system behavior, explaining more than 95% of the output variance. The high predictive accuracy observed across all surrogate models (), with most predictions within of CFD reference values, reflects the low‐dimensional character of the system, where the output is dominated by the Reynolds number. The trained models enable global sensitivity analysis through Monte Carlo simulation and real‐time prediction of cuttings velocity, supporting continuous monitoring, control, and optimization of borehole cleaning in deep drilling operations, while demonstrating how information from expensive high‐fidelity CFD simulations can be retained in fast, computationally cheap surrogates.

papers.title: An Innovative Long-Path Off-Axis DOAS System: High Light Throughput Design and Dedicated Spectral Processing Algorithm for Cl2 Monitoring
papers.abstract: This paper develops a novel long-path off-axis DOAS (LP-OA-DOAS) system integrated with an automatic spectral processing and concentration inversion algorithm. An asymmetric off-axis parabolic configuration is proposed to avoid central occlusion of coaxial structures. 1:1 comparative ray-tracing models are established for coaxial and off-axis setups to evaluate their optical performance. Ray-tracing simulations suggest that the off-axis layout offers potential advantages over the coaxial structure in terms of luminous flux transmission efficiency and alignment tolerance. On this basis, an LP-OA-DOAS system is developed. For spectral processing, a physics-informed neural network-based algorithm, termed DOAS-Cl 2 -PINN (Differential Optical Absorption Spectroscopy-based Physics-Informed Neural Network for Cl 2 inversion), is proposed to extract broad-band Cl 2 absorption features from spectra affected by environmental noise. CBAM (Convolutional Block Attention Module) is employed to adaptively enhance the representation of informative spectral features, while physical prior constraints based on the Beer-Lambert law are incorporated to improve the robustness of concentration inversion, physical consistency and enhance model interpretability. Controlled experiments were conducted using a gas cell with an effective Cl 2 absorption length of 133.86 mm positioned along a 200 m geometric open optical path. The proposed method accurately retrieved the gas-cell Cl 2 concentration, achieving an RMSE of 17.71 ppm and an R 2 of 0.99. Compared with the conventional least squares (LS) method used in DOAS analysis, the proposed method improved retrieval accuracy by 17.64% and consistently outperformed baseline models, including SVR, MLP, and 1D-CNN. Robustness analysis under varying environmental conditions further demonstrated stable retrieval performance under spectral disturbances and environmental variations. The calculated method detection limit of the LP-OA-DOAS system was 7.387 ppm·m, and measurement variations remained within ±5%. This detection limit corresponds to an equivalent minimum detectable concentration of 36.93 ppb, assuming a uniform Cl 2 distribution over the entire 200 m path. A six-month deployment in a liquid chlorine filling workshop demonstrated stable, fully automatic monitoring without false alarms under leakage-free operating conditions. Taken together, the controlled experimental results and field deployment support the system’s Cl 2 detection and concentration retrieval capabilities, as well as its operational stability. Its detection performance in actual industrial Cl 2 leakage scenarios warrants further validation under appropriate conditions.

papers.title: 3D printed spinal fusion devices: Technological breakthroughs, clinical challenges and intelligent future
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D)‑printed spinal fusion devices have emerged as a transformative solution to the limitations associated with conventional spinal implants, including mechanical mismatch, limited biocompatibility, and insufficient bioactivity. This review summarizes recent advances in the development of 3D‑printed spinal fusion devices and discusses how additive manufacturing technologies address key shortcomings of traditional implants. Recent evidence demonstrates that additive manufacturing enables the fabrication of patient‑specific implants with optimized porous architectures—such as triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) structures—that closely replicate the mechanical characteristics of native bone while promoting osseointegration. In addition, the integration of bioactive materials and functional coatings enhances biological performance and introduces multifunctional capabilities, including localized drug delivery and improved interface stability. Another important development is the application of artificial intelligence (AI) in implant design and surgical planning, enabling personalized structural optimization and biomechanical matching. Overall, the convergence of 3D printing and AI is accelerating the transition toward intelligent and personalized spinal implants with the potential to substantially improve surgical outcomes. However, widespread clinical translation will require long‑term safety validation, cost reduction, and the establishment of standardized regulatory frameworks.

papers.title: Physics-Data Co-driven Reliability-Based Robust Design for Rolling Bearings Under Small-Sample Uncertainty
papers.abstract: This study proposes a physics-data fusion framework for reliability assessment and reliability-based robust design of rolling bearings under small-sample uncertainty. Hertzian contact theory and finite element analysis (FEM) are integrated using inverse-variance weighted and Bayesian fusion strategies, followed by Gaussian Kriging surrogate modeling. L-moments are employed to characterize the unknown radial-load distribution from limited measurements, while asymmetric Gauss-Hermite quadrature is used to obtain the first four moments of the limit-state function. The Maximum Entropy Method (MEM) is then applied for reliability assessment, and a dual-surrogate-assisted NSGA-II framework is established to simultaneously minimize bearing mass and reliability sensitivity under R ≥ 0.999. Results show that Bayesian fusion achieves R2 = 0.9932 and an average relative error of 0.359% relative to FEM. Both Kriging models achieve R2 > 0.97 in leave-one-out cross-validation. The MEM results agree well with million-sample Monte Carlo simulation. The selected balanced compromise designs reduce bearing mass by 5.00% and 6.09% for weighted and Bayesian fusion, respectively, while satisfying R ≥ 0.999 and substantially reducing reliability sensitivity.

papers.title: Voltage Sensorless Control of Reduced-Order Elementary Super-Lift Luo Converter using Extended Kalman Filter
papers.abstract: Sensorless control approaches can enhance system reliability while reducing sensor cost in dc/dc converters. In this paper, an extended Kalman filter based voltage sensorless control system is proposed to estimate both the input and output voltages of an elementary super-lift Luo converter using a reduced-order model, thereby decreasing the number of sensors. To regulate the output voltage of the elementary super-lift Luo converter, a proportional-integral controller with a reduced number of tuning parameters is designed to minimize steady-state error. The proposed method is evaluated in the MATLAB/Simulink environment under stepwise input/output voltage variations and ramp input voltage variation. The voltage sensorless control system achieves high estimation accuracy with mean absolute error values of 0.2082 V (stepwise input voltage variation), 0.2272 V (stepwise output voltage variation), and 0.1620 V (ramp and stepwise input voltage variation) for the three test scenarios, respectively. In addition, the proportional-integral controller provides a settling time of approximately 55 ms while maintaining negligible steady-state error for all scenarios. The obtained results demonstrate that the proposed voltage sensorless control system provides accurate voltage estimation, robust dynamic performance, and reduced sensor dependency, making it a promising solution for high-performance and cost-effective dc/dc converter applications.

papers.title: Musical structure, micromotion, and adaptive gesture in instrumental performance: a critical cross-study synthesis
papers.abstract: This article presents an integrative synthesis of seven studies conducted within a research program on expert saxophone performance: five performer-centered observational, kinematic, and interview studies, complemented by two perceptual experiments. The studies are compared according to musical and task conditions, movement descriptors and scales, and evidential perspective. Rhythm and pitch were most consistently associated with movement. Faster or rhythmically denser passages were linked to shorter or more frequent actions, while rhythmic density increased knee-cycle frequency as amplitude decreased. Pitch contour accompanied recurrent flexion–extension patterns, and knee trajectories showed predictive temporal precedence relative to a modeled pitch-expectation profile. Under movement restriction, projected center-of-mass range, velocity, distance, and area decreased, whereas knee phase changes increased and specific postural-frequency measures remained comparatively stable. Three non-exclusive interpretations of persistent micromotion are considered: postural regulation, sensorimotor entrainment and prediction, and motor learning. On this basis, the paper proposes an adaptive, multidimensional model in which musical structure and task constraints selectively reorganize movement across dimensions and scales, while expressive, technical, postural, and communicative functions remain overlapping and context-dependent. The model provides an empirically grounded framework for causal experiments and learning interventions on the functions of performative movement.

papers.title: The Effectiveness of the 5Ps Model as an Active Learning Approach for Enhancing Learning Outcomes and Knowledge Construction among Thai Secondary Students
papers.abstract: To move beyond passive knowledge transfer, instructional design must enable learners to construct knowledge autonomously while addressing individual differences. This study aimed to: 1) develop an instructional model integrating Social Constructivism with Learning Styles to enhance learning outcomes and students' knowledge construction abilities, and 2) evaluate its systemic effectiveness. Using a research and development (R&D) framework, the investigation involved 102 Grade 8 students from four regions of Thailand, selected via multi-stage random sampling. Research instruments comprised the 5Ps Model, lesson plans, an achievement test, and a knowledge construction assessment. Data analyses utilized means, standard deviations, paired-samples t-tests, one-sample t-tests, one-way ANOVA, Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, Cohen’s d, and Cohen’s dz. Results indicated that the developed model was structurally valid and content-consistent. Students' post-test scores surpassed their pre-test scores significantly (p < .05), demonstrating a large effect size. Additionally, students' knowledge construction scores significantly exceeded the 70% proficiency threshold, with no significant regional variations observed in post-test outcomes. Qualitative interview data indicated that the model promoted active learning, knowledge co-construction, and the translation of concepts into real-world situations. The findings demonstrate that integrating Social Constructivism with flexible learning activity design systematically supports deep learning in diverse classroom contexts.

papers.title: Blind Precise Assembly: Proprioceptive Sim-to-Real Peg-in-Hole for Diverse Parts
papers.abstract: Every robot already carries high-resolution contact sensors: its own joints. Legged robots and humanoids exploit them to walk, run, and track whole-body motions without vision, but there the contacts are large and forceful. Is joint sensing also enough for precise, contact-rich assembly, where the robot must find a millimeter-scale opening, mesh gear teeth, or catch a thread through light contact? We study this question by training blind assembly policies that observe only a short history of joint positions, velocities, and their own actions, without visual, force, torque, or tactile sensing. The poses of both the fixture and the part are unknown to the policy, and the grasp is randomized substantially. The policy must therefore assemble the parts through contact, sensed exclusively through its own proprioception. Trained with reinforcement learning entirely in simulation over randomized parts, grasps, and contacts, such policies learn peg insertion, gear meshing, and nut threading. The peg insertion policy transfers zero-shot to the real world and inserts pegs of different shapes and sizes in 73% of trials. Controlled comparisons with matched visual policies in simulation show that blind policies generalize far better to unseen part shapes and sizes, though they can be slower. Training such policies needs thousands of different assemblies, each simulated with its clearance intact, so we also release an open-source generator that builds them procedurally from exact convex pieces for MuJoCo; it is more accurate and faster than convex decomposition or MuJoCo's signed-distance collision. Videos and interactive simulations are at https://younghyopark.me/blind-proprioceptive-assembly/.

papers.title: SparseMax-dSTL: Sound Robustness with Horizon-Independent Gradient Allocation for Temporal Logic Trajectory Optimization
papers.abstract: A gradient-based solver that enforces a Signal Temporal Logic (STL) specification uses a smooth approximation of its quantitative semantics, the robustness. In safety-critical trajectory optimization, this approximation must have two properties. First, it must be sound, that is, nonnegative only on trajectories that satisfy the specification. Second, at each temporal operator, the weight of its gradient on the violating samples must stay bounded away from zero, however long the horizon. The approximations in use, including the log-sum-exp, its sound variant, and the generalized-mean robustness, do not have both. We introduce lower approximations of the minimum and the maximum whose gradients are sparsemax projections, and we prove that the robustness built from them has both. It lies below the exact robustness and is therefore sound, and its error has a bound that is independent of the number of samples and known before optimization. The gradient of each approximation is exactly zero on every sample beyond a data-dependent threshold, so the weight on violating samples a gap beyond the others has a positive lower bound at every horizon. On a planar unicycle and on a seven-joint manipulator beside a person in simulation, the log-sum-exp approximation is positive on a violating trajectory. As the horizon of the manipulator's task grows from 10 to 80 s, the gradient weight of the sound variant on the violating samples falls from 0.22 to 0.04, while that of sparsemax stays at 1. In a constrained trajectory optimization of the unicycle, the constraint on the log-sum-exp robustness returns a violating trajectory, whereas the constraint on the sparsemax robustness returns a trajectory that satisfies the specification with the required margin.

papers.title: Self-Building Labs
papers.abstract: Self-driving laboratories (SDLs) accelerate scientific discovery by automating experimental execution and optimization. AI agents can increasingly propose new experiments, but existing SDLs can only run the procedures they were built for. Adapting them to a new experiment still takes extensive manual engineering, which makes laboratory flexibility the bottleneck for scaling discovery. We introduce the self-building laboratory (SBL), which designs, configures, and operates its own laboratory setup given a high-level scientific goal. SBL starts from whatever already exists, from an empty room to a working SDL, and builds the missing capabilities: the lab layout, its digital twin, robot skills, and experimental workflows. We demonstrate the system working across different robots and setups, scaling from a single workstation to laboratories with several robots working together. We validate SBL's end-to-end capabilities through a real-world quantum-dot synthesis experiment. By shifting the role of human researchers from manually configuring and programming device automation to specifying scientific objectives, SBL makes scientific automation more accessible, flexible, and scalable. Project website: https://self-building-labs.github.io/

papers.title: Persistent Planar Memory for Video World Models
papers.abstract: Video world models that generate and explore environments at scale need a persistent 3D memory of what they have produced. Plane primitives offer a natural candidate: a compact set of oriented planes captures the dominant structural elements (e.g., walls, floors, facades) of indoor and outdoor scenes, while requiring only 7 parameters per primitive. We present PPMem, a video world model that adopts plane primitives as its persistent 3D memory. PPMem augments a video diffusion transformer with a planar prediction head and a Depth Token Fusion (DTF) module: each autoregressive chunk jointly produces RGB video and planar geometry, which merges into a persistent plane memory that conditions subsequent chunks via rendered depth. The resulting memory is three orders of magnitude more compact than per-pixel point clouds (~100K primitives, 5MB for a full scene), geometrically explicit (metric depth, normals, exportable surfaces), cross-view consistent (jointly predicted by the shared backbone), and adaptive (refined by the merging procedure as generation proceeds). On DL3DV and RealEstate10K, PPMem outperforms prior 3D-grounded world models in video quality while jointly producing metric-scale depth, surface normals, and exportable planar geometry, sustaining coherence across hundreds of frames under large viewpoint changes. Project page: https://hyzcluster.github.io/ppmem.

papers.title: Active Learning for Interatomic Potentials: A Review of Uncertainty-Driven Data Efficiency
papers.abstract: Developing a machine learning interatomic potential (MLIP) that is accurate for the specific conditions under which it will be applied, rather than simply for the predefined configurations chosen by the model developer, is a significant challenge in atomistic simulation. Active learning (AL) addresses this challenge by closing the loop between candidate generation, data selection, reference calculation, and model updating. Here, we survey more than seventy studies, with an emphasis on work from 2020 to 2026, to understand how active learning has evolved from a niche, on-the-fly training technique for query-by-committee and Gaussian process force fields into a diverse family of data-efficient strategies. he reviewed examples include on-the-fly molecular dynamics, active data selection for fine-tuning pretrained models, kernel- and representation-based acquisition using frozen pretrained models, and reaction-aware sampling for chemical systems far from equilibrium. We explore the use of active learning in elemental and alloy mechanics, hydrogen and ion diffusion, ferroelectrics and effective Hamiltonians of functional materials, reactive and photochemical dynamics, high-entropy and compositionally disordered materials, as well as generative and autonomous material discovery pipelines. Drawing on a growing body of critical, methodologically self-aware literature, we also show that this achievement carries systematic caveats. Uncertainty estimates are not interchangeable across model architectures and are frequently the least reliable exactly where they matter most. We close by discussing the outlook for standardized, uncertainty-calibrated, and observable-targeted active-learning workflows in the foundation-model era.

papers.title: Localizing and quantifying cerebral arterial stenosis from sparse velocity waveforms using a conditional neural operator
papers.abstract: Cerebral arterial stenosis alters blood flow throughout the vascular network, complicating the estimation of its location and severity from sparse velocity observations. We developed a conditional neural operator that predicts cerebral hemodynamics for candidate stenoses and enables inverse estimation through waveform comparison. Training data were generated using a sequential 0D-1D model that simulates pressure, cross-sectional area, and velocity under varying anatomical, physiological, and stenosis conditions. The operator encodes a single stenosis within vessel tokens and uses global attention to represent its effects across the network. Severity-gated coupling connects these representations to a shared field decoder, while paired healthy simulations constrain baseline predictions. After training, model weights remain fixed, and stenosis location and severity are estimated by minimizing the mismatch between predicted and observed midpoint velocity waveforms. Network-averaged relative validation errors were 0.14% for pressure, 0.59% for area, and 2.79% for velocity. For an eight-vessel observation configuration, localization accuracy across 20 candidate vessels was 99.4% without added noise and 96.0% at the 30% noise setting. Comparisons between configurations with equal numbers of observed vessels showed that measurement placement influenced recovery. Errors and localization ambiguities were greater in selected communicating and distal arteries. These results demonstrate the feasibility of surrogate-based stenosis estimation in simulated cerebral networks and highlight the importance of observation placement. Evaluation was limited to unseen stenosis scenarios within sampled anatomical and physiological conditions. Generalization to new individuals and clinical measurements requires further investigation.

papers.title: Not All Actions Contribute Equally: Learning Precise Progress Estimation from Imprecise Demonstrations
papers.abstract: Progress estimators play an essential role in providing dense reward signals for reinforcement learning in robotic manipulation, but accurately assessing task progress can be much challenging. Existing methods heavily rely on expert data and naively assume that all actions within a demonstration contribute to task success. This assumption often breaks down in real-world scenarios, especially in high-precision manipulation, where subtle geometric errors can lead to task failure. Therefore, these methods can erroneously interpret human mistakes as meaningful progress, further corrupting progress learning. We argue that a key limitation is the lack of a global prior regarding task evaluation criteria, which is crucial for distinguishing meaningful progress from human mistakes. To this end, we propose PRIME, a novel progress estimator capable of learning precise progress estimation from imprecise demonstrations by aggregating experience across trajectories. PRIME constructs a weighted graph over observed states, connecting states across trajectories based on spatial proximity and visual consistency. Edge weights encode spatial distances as transition costs, and shortest-path search approximates the geodesic distance to success. Changes in this distance naturally distinguish advancement, stagnation, and setbacks without assuming monotonic progress over time. Extensive experiments in both simulation and real world on precise manipulation tasks show that PRIME is consistently effective across diverse tasks, and robust to data with varying degrees of suboptimality. Notably, the advantage of PRIME gets more pronounced in higher-precision scenarios, yielding up to a \(5\times\) improvement in policy success rate over the SFT baselines on charger insertion.

papers.title: Beyond Large Language Models: A Mental World Model Framework for Mental Modeling, Simulation, Evolution, and Interpretability
papers.abstract: Understanding and simulating how subjective cognition and mental states emerge, evolve, and shape behavior is essential for advancing artificial intelligence toward deeper social cognition and general intelligence. Existing large language models (LLMs) and Theory of Mind (ToM) methods primarily infer mental states from linguistic information, lacking unified mechanisms for subjective world construction, cognitive-psychological interactions, dynamic evolution, and historical dependencies. This paper introduces the Mental World Model (MWM) and its implementation, the Multi-Branch Mental Evolution Architecture (MMEA), which explicitly constructs subjective worlds, models interactions between cognition and mental states, and simulates continuous mental evolution shaped by historical experiences. On DynToM and RecToM, MMEA achieves 96.48% and 94.00% accuracy, respectively, outperforming leading LLMs and specialized ToM methods. Additional experiments demonstrate improvements of 28.7, 39.3, and 16.6 percentage points in mental state and behavior prediction, long-sequence prediction, and implicit mental state inference, respectively. The results demonstrate that MMEA provides an interpretable framework for continuous mental modeling, enabling AI to move beyond surface-level semantic representations to infer individuals' underlying mental states from linguistic information and dynamically simulate their internal cognitive processes and evolution over time. MWM also provides a promising foundation for causal reasoning, personalized AI, sustained human-AI interaction, and future advances toward artificial general intelligence (AGI).

papers.title: Deconstructing Multi-Task Active Learning: The Paradox of Gradient Conflict and Orthogonal Decomposition
papers.abstract: Existing multi-task active learning (MTL-AL) methods predominantly rely on linear scalarization of heterogeneous objectives such as uncertainty, diversity, and gradient conflict. We argue that this entangled formulation is fundamentally limited, as linear combination fails to capture Pareto-optimal trade-offs under conflicting objectives. We propose a shift from combination to deconstruction and introduce a principled framework that rethinks MTL-AL along three orthogonal dimensions. First, we identify the Conflict Paradox: although the optimization literature treats gradient conflict as interference to be suppressed, penalizing conflict when ranking candidates is measurably worse than not scoring it at all. We therefore decouple the two concerns: the acquisition function does not score conflict, and the resulting interference is resolved by gradient surgery during training. Second, we introduce Orthogonal Decomposition, separating acquisition into Informativeness and Exploration. This two-stage process, informativeness filtering followed by coverage maximization, prevents "diversity dilution" by excluding uninformative outliers before enforcing diversity. Third, we propose Cross-Task Mutual Information (CTMI), a covariance-based statistic of cross-task dependency computed from MC-dropout task entropies. Extensive experiments on COCO, Cityscapes, and NYUv2, including comparisons against recent MTL-AL and data-selection baselines, demonstrate consistent improvements over state-of-the-art methods, highlighting that structural rethinking of acquisition yields larger gains than incremental heuristic design. Code is available at https://github.com/Juho-Jung/multitask_active_learning_official.

papers.title: Causal Discovery beyond Conditional Independence: Identifiability, Algorithms, and Statistical Inference for Directed Acyclic and Cyclic Graphs
papers.abstract: Learning causal structure from data requires assumptions about mechanisms, noises, observation schemes, and interventions. Historically, causal discovery has relied primarily on conditional independence. This review focuses on modern causal discovery methods that exploit properties of distributions beyond conditional independence. Our organizing principle separates the source of identification from the statistical estimator and its computational implementation. This perspective connects conditional-independence methods with distributional asymmetries, conditional-moment restrictions, and variation across environments or individuals. We examine discovery under latent confounding and feedback, distinguishing causal information about observed variables from reconstruction of latent structure and emphasizing the additional semantics required by cyclic models. We also distinguish population identification, frequentist and Bayesian consistency, uncertainty quantification, and algorithmic guarantees. Throughout, examples show why the same observational distribution can support different conclusions under different model classes. We conclude with guidance for comparing methods at their identifiable targets and a research agenda for uncertainty, heterogeneous populations, non-scalar variables, and the intersection of discrete data, feedback, and hidden confounding.

papers.title: Execution Before Memory: Diagnosing Memory Failures in Video World Models
papers.abstract: A memory test for a video world model should say whether the scene was set, whether the asked change was carried out, and whether the last frame shows the result. Current tests fold these into one number, so a low score is easy to read as forgetting. When the change is not carried out, the hidden state transition cannot appear, so the test is not really a test of memory. We introduce MIST, an evaluation that separates the change from the memory it should leave behind. The model first sets the scene while the change stays hidden, and only later is asked to show it, with leakage before that point kept under control. This separation locates the bottleneck: the model sets the scene but does not carry out the instructed change. The same gap appears in general memory evaluations. On that basis we propose M3-Agent (Make the Missing Move), which recursively revises the details of the input instruction so that the model successfully carries out the requested instruction. Relative to the baseline, it more than triples the MIST reveal score. On the benchmarks, WRBench's score T rises by 26.1% and MBench-T's score U by 52.7%. The method meets the problem from the execution side: it shows what the frozen model can do once the move is stated, and it sets a stricter baseline.

papers.title: Adaptive conformal prediction on the Grassmannian
papers.abstract: We introduce a conformal prediction framework for regression with Grassmann-valued responses. The proposed method constructs prediction regions in the form of metric balls directly on the Grassmann manifold, using basis-invariant geometric distances as non-conformity measures and scaling the corresponding non-conformity scores through a learned prediction difficulty estimator. This yields locally adaptive, input-dependent prediction regions that respect the underlying manifold geometry, while retaining the finite-sample marginal coverage guarantee of split conformal prediction under exchangeability. We evaluate several Grassmannian distance metrics and compare their prediction-region efficiency on synthetic benchmarks and an airfoil inverse shape-design problem. The results highlight the advantages of geometry-aware non-conformity scores, while local adaptation improves empirical coverage uniformity across prediction difficulty levels and, in strongly heteroscedastic settings, can substantially reduce prediction-region size while maintaining the target coverage.

papers.title: A Structure-Preserving Semi-Lagrangian based bi-fidelity method for the Vlasov--Poisson system with uncertainties
papers.abstract: Uncertainty quantification for the Vlasov--Poisson (VP) systems entails repeated dynamic simulations, incurring immense computational costs. We develop a structure-preserving Semi-Lagrangian (SL) b-fidelity approximation of macroscopic observables. The MUSCL is used as a low-fidelity solver for pressureless Euler--Poisson system, allowing for a more cost-effective exploration of the stochastic parameter space. A conservative SL scheme combined with high-order discontinuous Galerkin is used as a high-fidelity solver for collisionless VP system, whose mass conservation, positivity preservation, and low numerical dissipation provide a more reliable high-fidelity snapshots for bi-fidelity reconstruction. We further derive a conditional error bound that separates projection, discretization, and model errors. Numerical experiments for both deterministic and uncertain VP problems, including multispecies and higher-dimensional settings, demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves accurate and robust uncertainty propagation.

papers.title: Towards optimal selection schedules for online active learning
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of online linear classification, where a stream of unlabeled samples is available, and annotation is costly. We investigate the optimal query policy, that prescribes whether and when a sample should be labeled and used for a training step, or instead discarded, so as to minimize a given objective. We focus on the realizable case, under Gaussian design, in the high-dimensional regime where data dimension and number of unlabeled samples grow proportionally. We consider two objectives: 1) the generalization error under a labeling budget, and 2) a cumulative cost function where mistakes have unit cost and queries cost $Δ$. We first show that the myopic policies that greedily minimize at all times the increment in the objective correspond to either small or intermediate-margin policies, that prescribe the selection of samples whose margins fall within certain intervals that shrink with time. Within this class, we numerically ascertain the optimal schedules for the selection thresholds that minimize the final values of the objectives. Taking inspiration from the myopic policy for the cumulative cost, we design a very simple query policy schedule that we compare to other proposed heuristics, on synthetic data and real medical image datasets. Finally, we discuss myopic policies for two-layer neural networks, and exemplify how naive margin-based policies can cease to be optimal.

papers.title: Reinforcement Learning-Based Pricing and Operation for Hybrid Electric and Hydrogen Vehicle Stations
papers.abstract: Electric vehicles (EVs) and hydrogen fuel cell vehi- cles (HFCVs) are promising technologies in the efforts to reduce carbon emissions. Challenges such as limited infrastructure, con- sumer dissatisfaction, and electrical grid strain inhibit progress in the adoption of these technologies. A zero emission vehicle (ZEV) station, capable of handling EVs and HFCVs, addresses these challenges by focusing on maximizing station profit and consumer utility, while minimizing grid impacts. The purpose of this research is to develop a realistic simulation of a ZEV station that is capable of handling real-time pricing decisions enabled by reinforcement learning (RL) and to compare the performance of the RL agent to static pricing methods. After training, the RL agent gains 10.83% greater station profit than the baseline manual parameter search. This work serves as a useful tool for ZEV station owners when handling complex pricing and purchasing decisions.

papers.title: Predictable Scaling: Efficient Model Exploration via Scaling-Law Prediction
papers.abstract: Evaluating candidate changes (hypotheses) to recommendation models requires full-scale training runs consuming thousands of GPU-hours, severely limiting the hypothesis space engineers can feasibly explore. We introduce Predictable Scaling (PS), a systematic framework that exploits empirically verified regularity conditions to predict full-scale model performance from small-scale proxies. PS constructs scaled-down variants via composable scaling functions along distinct resource axes, and projects metrics to the target scale via curve fitting with calibrated uncertainty estimates. We compare three prediction strategies of increasing expressiveness: even the simplest (raw proxy) achieves prediction error within the empirical noise floor of repeated-run variance; the most expressive (Gaussian Process) provides an indicative 15% relative MAE improvement and calibrated uncertainty. Evaluation on two ranking models of increasing complexity---a task-specific model and a foundation model---demonstrates that PS correctly ranks actionable hypotheses across diverse hypothesis types at 79-88% compute reductions.

papers.title: RECREG: Recovery-based Shielding for Regular Safety Properties in Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: In many real-world scenarios we need to consider formal requirements, such as safety and constraint compliance, to deploy Reinforcement Learning (RL) agents. In this paper we introduce RecReg, a safe RL framework capable of enforcing non-Markovian regular safety properties via recovery-based shielding. RecReg is a unified approach that supports different levels of a priori knowledge and safety guarantees. The paper primarily focuses on building the theoretical foundations for RecReg in the tabular setting, providing rigorous safety and convergence guarantees that are not present in related work. We provide an extensive set of empirical results using the MASA-Safe-RL library, and we outline an extension of RecReg to deep RL domains using SOTA model-based RL. Our empirical results demonstrate that RecReg achieves efficient learning and matches the theory in this paper.
