papers.title: No Eyes, No Problem: What Does Touch Contribute to Blind Baoding Ball Manipulation?
papers.abstract: Humans manipulate objects within their hands through touch alone with remarkable ease, but for robots, achieving sustained real-world manipulation without vision remains an open challenge. Although reinforcement learning (RL) can generate sophisticated blind manipulation policies in simulation, transferring them to a real dexterous hand remains hindered by continuously changing contacts, motion-induced tactile information drift, and the gap between simulated and physical dynamics. We study this problem through Baoding ball rotation on the Shadow Dexterous Hand Lite, using only proprioception and binary tactile feedback as observations. We achieve successful zero-shot transfer through a combination of a sensor-aligned, coupling-aware embodiment in simulation, tactile calibration, and two novel episodic domain randomisations: slew-rate action limits and STuck-AT Taxels. On the physical hand, the policy achieves sustained blind Baoding rotation, completing 225 consecutive $\mathbf{180^\circ}$ rotations (112.5 full rotations) at $\sim0.36 \;\text{rot/s}$ in a single continuous trial without any vision or object-state information. Furthermore, we evaluate the contribution of tactile sensing relative to proprioception alone and identify the hand regions where tactile information is most important. This is the strongest reported hardware result for Baoding ball manipulation in both rotation count and speed, irrespective of the sensing modality used. By effectively bridging the sim-to-real gap, our framework sets a new benchmark for sustained tactile-driven dexterous manipulation on physical hardware.

papers.title: Hydrogen Ion-Cut Single-Crystal Diamond Membranes for Wide and Ultrawide Bandgap Semiconductor Heterointegration
papers.abstract: Single-crystal diamond membranes (SCDms) were created using a hydrogen ion-cut process combined with a two-step post-implantation annealing, electrochemical etching, and micro-transfer printing. Monte Carlo simulations comparing H, He, C, and O implantation predicted a narrower vacancy-distribution profile for hydrogen under the implantation conditions examined. Raman spectroscopy was used to evaluate implantation-induced lattice damage and its recovery during annealing and membrane release, while optical bandgap analysis provided further evidence of restoration of the diamond lattice structure. After delamination and removal of residual graphitic material, freestanding SCDms with improved crystalline quality were obtained. The SCDms were subsequently transferred to GaN, SiC, AlGaN, and AlN substrates without an adhesive layer. The successful formation of diamond/WBG and diamond/UWBG heterostructures demonstrates the feasibility of integrating the SCDms with a range of semiconductor platforms. Overall, these results establish hydrogen implantation as an effective route for producing high-quality SCDms for future diamond-based heterogeneous integration applications.

papers.title: LithoWorld: An Endpoint World Model for Lithography Process-Window Recovery
papers.abstract: Lithography process drift can move a fabricated pattern outside its process window, producing unqualified scanning electron microscopy (SEM) morphology. We present LithoWorld, an endpoint world model for SEM-guided parameter recovery. Interior representative targets jointly determine qualified reference appearance and correction supervision. A causal predictive branch aligns currentimage features with endpoint representations, while a conditional flow policy generates a two-dimensional correction as an action chunk. The model learns from 173 groups of measured SEMs organized as focus-exposure maps, preserving unmeasured cells as unknown. On 200 test pairs from the 73-group subset, LithoWorld achieves 88.5% qualified-region success and 46.0% interior success, exceeding the strongest comparison method by 2.5 and 6.0 percentage points, respectively. Ablations separate the effects of target selection, endpoint alignment, and output parameterization. Qualitative SEM retrieval illustrates recovery to qualified interiors without requiring exact reference-coordinate matching.

papers.title: AWAM: Active Trajectory-Conditioned View Imagination for Robust Robot Manipulation
papers.abstract: Rapid progress in embodied intelligence has enabled increasingly capable robots to follow language instructions and manipulate diverse objects. However, strong results in structured environments do not automatically transfer to open-world conditions, where clutter, occlusion, and changing viewpoints can obscure the spatial relationships required for action. To address this perceptual gap, a virtual active-perception paradigm is introduced. AWAM, an Active World-Action Model actively plans where to observe and imagines what will be seen along the planned trajectory before acting. Task-related virtual camera motion is predicted and used as a structured query into a geometry-conditioned world model, producing a reusable spatial prior for manipulation, which is later compressed into a fixed memory and fused with live observations through cross-attention for diffusion-based action prediction. AWAM achieves competitive success rates with 75.9% on LIBERO-Occ, 62.4% on LIBERO-Plus, 76.5% on RLBench-OG Occlusion1, and 94.4% in real-robot trials. These results support improved robustness to the evaluated occlusions and distribution shifts, addressing part of the gap between structured manipulation and less controlled environments.

papers.title: Language Models Learn to Improve Language Models
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to automate AI research, including language-model (LM) development, offering a potential path toward recursive self-improvement. However, turning experimental feedback into a learned ability to propose effective improvements across models faces two challenges. First, training such an ability with real feedback is expensive: reinforcement learning (RL) requires evaluating tens of thousands of proposals, each potentially requiring a full model-training run. Even at ten GPU-hours per run, reward collection alone would consume hundreds of thousands of GPU-hours, motivating a cheaper surrogate. Second, surrogate feedback can become unreliable as policy optimization favors overestimated proposals when the proposal distribution shifts. To address these challenges, we propose LM2LM, which trains LLMs with RL to generate effective LM improvement proposals. To provide scalable feedback, we use a research world model (RWM), a frozen LLM that predicts proposal gains from real experimental records provided in context, as the reward model for RL. To maintain feedback reliability, we periodically execute current-policy proposals ranked highly by the RWM and add their measured outcomes to its context. Across eight autoregressive and diffusion LM development environments, real-execution evaluations on held-out tasks show that LM2LM enables Qwen3.8-27B to outperform GPT-6-sol, even when GPT-6-sol is given 300 real experimental records in context, while requiring 33% lower data-generation cost. LM2LM also generalizes to a model family unseen during training.

papers.title: How the elastic axis folds the transonic flutter boundary: shock energy transfer and conformally calibrated active learning
papers.abstract: Isogai's case A, a pitch-plunge aerofoil whose elastic axis lies half a chord ahead of the leading edge, has a folded transonic flutter boundary in inviscid flow: near the bottom of the transonic dip several flutter speeds coexist at one Mach number. We map this boundary, and the family obtained by moving the elastic axis, with coupled unsteady Euler simulations, a Gaussian-process surrogate of the damping coefficient trained by batch active learning, and split conformal prediction on independent random simulations, which turns the surrogate into stability calls with a distribution-free error rate. Three failure modes of time-domain damping labels that leave no trace in the residuals are documented, and the half-degree mean incidence left by the common one-degree start is shown to raise the flutter speed at the dip by 2.8%, more than any numerical setting. With 80 simulations the learned case A boundary labels 64 of 65 independent runs correctly, and calibrated calls are wrong in at most 1.6% of cases. Over Mach number, elastic axis and flutter speed index, 193 simulations and 40 calibration runs show that the fold exists only for elastic axes more than about 0.4 chord ahead of the leading edge; it closes between 0.39 and 0.33 chord ahead, on two meshes. Chordwise energy budgets, closed against the solver loads and the growth rate within a few per cent, explain the boundary. The lower branch is crossed through the reduced frequency at unchanged shock phase. On the upper branch the shock is pinned at the trailing edge, and moving the elastic axis aft brings the pivot of the flutter mode towards the section, so that the damping of the supersonic surface falls faster than the residual shock input and the fold closes.

papers.title: Multilevel Gaussian Processes with Applications to Inverse Problems
papers.abstract: We present a multilevel Gaussian process (GP) regression framework for approximating functions that are accessible only through a hierarchy of approximations of increasing accuracy and computational cost. One example is the response surface of a parametrized partial differential equation, where the hierarchy arises from the resolution of the numerical solver. Modeling level increments independently with Matérn-kernel GPs and allocating samples flexibly across discretization levels yields substantial computational savings over single-level GP regression. We derive $L^2$ convergence rates for the posterior mean and variance, accounting for maximum likelihood estimation of the marginal variance and for kernel misspecification. When increment regularity or solver cost is unknown a priori, an adaptive sequential-design algorithm with cost-adapted active learning criteria allocates samples across levels. We apply the surrogate to Bayesian inverse problems, for which Hellinger distance bounds between the true and approximate posteriors are known. Numerical experiments illustrate the theoretical rates and the resulting computational savings.

papers.title: Nondimensionalization, Variational Inequalities and Uncertainty Quantification in a Morphoelastic Model for Burn Injury Healing
papers.abstract: Mathematical modelling of burn injury healing involves coupling biological processes with mechanical deformation, resulting in computationally stiff, nonlinear partial differential equations that severely limit the scalability of existing numerical solutions. We present a computational framework addressing these challenges. By nondimensionalizing the model and performing scaling analysis, we show that chemotaxis and inertia are negligible, permitting a quasi-static momentum approach. To enforce non-negativity constraints, we implement a Variational Inequality formulation using the Finite Element Method in FEniCSx, and verify it via numerical convergence studies and mass balances. We identify high-order parameter interactions, specifically equilibrium collagen density and signalling dynamics, as the primary drivers of solver stability. A sensitivity analysis of nearly four million simulations reveals that isolated parameter variations predominantly govern the maximum wound contraction. In contrast, higher-order interactions determine the timing of maximum contraction and the permanent contracture. However, no significant pairwise parameter interactions were found, suggesting that the model's behaviour is governed by higher-order interactions, highlighting the inherent complexity of the wound-healing process.

papers.title: ORD-WM: Learning Object-Centric Rigid Dynamics for 3D World Modeling in Robotic Manipulation
papers.abstract: World models provide robots with a predictive mechanism for reasoning about how actions change object states in manipulation tasks. However, existing image-based and dense 3D world models do not explicitly impose object-level rigid motion, leaving rigid-object geometry preservation to be learned implicitly and making multi-step rollouts susceptible to shape drift or object-level motion inconsistency. To address this, we propose ORD-WM, a 3D world model that learns object-centric rigid dynamics for robotic manipulation. ORD-WM learns a vector-neuron variational autoencoder supervised by signed distance fields, which encodes each object point cloud as a geometry-aware latent representation composed of 3D vector features, and uses an action-conditioned dynamics model to predict object-wise SE(3) motion increments. Rather than generating unconstrained next latent states, ORD-WM analytically applies predicted object-wise rigid transformations to the current latent states, separating persistent object geometry from pose changes. Experiments show that ORD-WM enables stable, geometry-preserving multi-step prediction and supports efficient real-time replanning for closed-loop model predictive control in simulated and real-world manipulation scenarios.

papers.title: BeJEPA: A Goal-Conditioned Humanoid Behavior World Model via Unsupervised RL
papers.abstract: Humanoid control requires coordinating whole-body posture with position and heading in the world frame. Mainstream controllers imitate trajectories in the root frame, but struggle to regain the target world pose after displacement. We introduce BeJEPA, a goal-conditioned Behavior World Model learned through unsupervised reinforcement learning from human motion priors and robot interaction. BeJEPA learns a shared representation of body configuration and world placement through a joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA). A Dynamic Predictor predicts the next state embedding under an action, while a Successor Predictor summarizes a goal-conditioned policy's expected discounted future state embeddings in a single vector. During joint training, Dynamic grounds the initial representation in observed physical transitions, while Successor increasingly organizes it around long-term behavior. Their composition guides policy improvement through one physical prediction and one behavioral summary, without long imagined rollouts. In 20-second motion-tracking experiments, BeJEPA with online action refinement using Dynamic outperforms all evaluated baselines in global body-position error, reducing it on AMASS by 61.7% relative to BFM-Zero with world-pose inputs and 58.7% relative to SONIC. Physical deployment on a Unitree G1 demonstrates joint attainment of posture, world position, and heading goals, recovery from the ground, and closed-loop return after disturbances and goal changes. Project page: https://ylyem9x.github.io/BeJEPA-project.

papers.title: Agentic In-Context Learning: What Algorithms Can Transformers Learn in Closed-Loop Interaction?
papers.abstract: The learning algorithm view of in-context learning (ICL) studies how fixed-parameter Transformers learn from supplied examples. Language model agents extend this setting through interaction: their actions determine what evidence enters context next. We call this regime Agentic In-Context Learning (Agentic ICL). Existing studies largely depend on externally supplied contexts or reward-bearing interaction histories, while work on general tool-using agents lacks a learning algorithm view. We represent an interactive learner by its state, update, and decision rule, covering active learning, bandits, and online reinforcement learning (RL). For expressivity, we construct causal Transformers that approximate these algorithms over a finite horizon, and bound the resulting loss in return. For training, we characterize when optimizing process rewards preserves behavior that maximizes the final outcome. Distillation experiments show that Transformers can learn to execute three representative recursions. We then train models from outcome or process rewards without oracle action or state targets, as in RL post-training. Different rewards yield distinct decision policies. Improving the alignment of process supervision with outcome-optimal action preferences shifts learned decisions accordingly. Such behavioral differences persist in a pretrained language model across textual paraphrases.

papers.title: Ego2Contact: Predicting Touch from Egocentric Human Video for Contact-Rich Robot Manipulation
papers.abstract: Contact locations and interaction forces are critical for contact-rich robot manipulation but are often ambiguous from vision alone. Measuring them on robots requires specialized tactile hardware and platform-specific data collection, which keeps robot tactile data scarce. Human egocentric video is far easier to scale but lacks touch. Recent predictors trained on egocentric recordings paired with tactile-glove measurements can predict this missing signal from video alone. These predictors, however, remain confined to human hands, which differ from robot hands in appearance and tactile layout. We present Ego2Contact, which learns a visual-tactile prior from human interactions and transfers it to robot hands. Its predictor fuses temporal scene context with hand-local visual features to infer bimanual tactile fields from the RGB video. Anatomical region correspondences align varying robot tactile layouts with the predictor's canonical grid, turning robot measurements into fine-tuning targets and predictions into policy inputs. Ego2Contact outperforms prior tactile predictors on human data, including unseen objects, and on robot data after adaptation. The adapted predictor provides tactile inputs for both simulated reinforcement learning and real-robot policy post-training. In simulation, policies using predicted touch outperform non-tactile baselines and recover part of the benefit of ground-truth tactile sensing. These results show that human-learned tactile priors can supply touch when direct tactile sensing is limited.

papers.title: PINN-LPCDD: Physics-Informed Neural Network with Learnable and Physically Consistent Domain Decomposition for Compressible Multi-Medium Flows
papers.abstract: The physics-informed neural network (PINN) faces significant challenges when solving compressible multi-medium flows, including the inability to locate interface positions, poor approximation of discontinuities, and difficulty in handling high-pressure-ratio problems between media with large stiffness differences. To address these issues, we propose PINN with Learnable and Physically Consistent Domain Decomposition (PINN-LPCDD), a framework that incorporates the sharp interface method (SIM) into PINNs for solving compressible multi-medium flows. Firstly, we design separate sub-networks for each medium with learnable parameters to automatically learn interface positions, so that the domain decomposition is physically consistent, and the contact discontinuity at the interface is naturally sharp. Secondly, the Euler equations with artificial viscosity are solved to enhance robustness when handling problems involving shock waves. Lastly, the scaling invariance of the Euler equations is exploited to facilitate the solution of high pressure ratio problems. Numerical experiments on air-air, air-helium, air-water, and air-R22 problems demonstrate the acceptable accuracy of the proposed method in simulating multi-medium flows.

papers.title: Acquisition Function-Guided Generation for Bayesian Optimization over Discrete Spaces
papers.abstract: Bayesian optimization (BO) over discrete spaces is challenging due to missing gradients and the sparsity of valid solutions. Latent-space BO sidesteps both issues by fitting a surrogate in the latent space of a generative model, which however substantially complicates the direct incorporation of domain knowledge that is naturally expressed in the original discrete space. In this work, we instead combine a pretrained generative model with a surrogate defined directly in data space, where inductive biases such as domain-specific kernels can be readily incorporated. Rather than maximizing the acquisition function over the discrete design space, our method samples candidates from the generative model under a distribution tilted by the acquisition function. To recover useful gradients for sampling, we embed this tilted distribution into a diffusion bridge that yields a smooth, posterior-averaged acquisition function. This leads to \emph{acquisition function guided generation} (AFGG), which we instantiate with a categorical diffusion model and an autoregressive normalizing flow. Across a broad suite of molecular benchmarks, the diffusion model variant performs on par with leading BO methods, while the flow model variant outperforms state-of-the-art methods in most cases and remains highly competitive otherwise. Our implementation is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/afgg.

papers.title: Necrosis avascular bilateral de la cabeza del fémur
papers.abstract: Avascular necrosis of the femoral head results from disrupted blood supply leading to bone death and joint collapse.We report the case of a 60-year-old man with chronic kidney disease on hemodialysis, with diabetes mellitus and hypertension, without trauma or corticosteroid exposure. He presented with progressive bilateral hip pain and functional limitation. Radiographs revealed subchondral cysts and bilateral femoral head collapse consistent with advanced avascular necrosis of the femoral head. Chronic kidney disease-related hypoxia, metabolic abnormalities, and uremic toxins likely contributed to osteonecrosis. Bilateral total hip arthroplasty in staged procedures was recommended.This case emphasizes the need to consider this type of necrosis in hemodialysis patients presenting with non-traumatic hip pain, especially given the rare and clinically significant bilateral involvement, which severely impacts mobility and quality of life.

papers.title: Teacher Performance Management through Continuous Professional Development in Madrasahs
papers.abstract: This narrative literature synthesis examines how madrasahs might connect teacher performance management with continuous professional development. The supplied manuscript proposes a four-part cycle: setting performance goals and mapping competency needs; providing sustained professional learning; observing instruction and offering developmental feedback; and revising practice in light of evidence and Islamic educational values. Research on effective teacher learning supports coherent content, active learning, collaboration, and repeated opportunities to apply new practices, while work on supervision highlights the role of feedback. A madrasah may use these insights to connect pedagogical and professional competencies with its Islamic educational mission. The source describes searches and thematic analysis but does not report databases, search dates, screening counts, a complete study set, appraisal, or a reproducible synthesis. The four dimensions are therefore a proposed conceptual framework, not a demonstrated effect of a particular program. Implementation should be assessed through observed instructional change, teacher feedback, and student evidence before claims of improved performance are made.

papers.title: Robust Stability Analysis and PINN-Based Monitoring for Hybrid Power Systems Under Heavy Loading Constraints
papers.abstract: In this paper, the IEEE 39-bus system is used to analyze stability limits for hybrid power systems at high load levels. Consensus diagram via Participation Factor analysis identifies critical oscillations from generators G6 and G7 to exceed a 1.7 load factor, introducing Right-Half Plane poles that will impair control performance (Waterbed Effect). Applying a solid analytical approach, we demonstrate that the system physics limits the sensitivity peak. This is a warning indicator created by a Physics-Informed Neural Network trained on eigenvalue data. Simulations assure that it can accurately mark the most critical nodes as risky nodes and provide a theoretical stability limit, allowing more reliable integration of Inverter-Based Resources in smart grids.

papers.title: Lifting Safety Through Reduced-Order Model Architectures: An Invariant Manifold Approach
papers.abstract: Reduced-order model architectures are often used to decompose complex safety-critical control design tasks into tractable subproblems. In this paradigm, one must ask: when does the safety of a reduced-order model lift to safety of the full system? Taking an invariant manifold perspective, we provide necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of smooth, regular lifts of compact safe sets from reduced-order models. Our characterization relies only on asymptotic stability of an embedding of a reduced-order safe set, without additional robustness or rate conditions. We apply these results to study control barrier functions in reduced-order model architectures and lifts of safe sets through cascades. Further, we use our conditions to obtain topological obstructions to the tracking of safe, kinematic reduced-order models for mechanical systems. We conclude by using these obstructions to inform safe hierarchical control design for an underactuated satellite on SE(3).

papers.title: An important Bottleneck in LLM Optimizers: Principle-Level Local Optima
papers.abstract: Feedback-driven LLM optimizers are increasingly used for evolutionary search, Bayesian optimization, heuristic design, and scientific discovery. Yet rapid initial gains often give way to prolonged plateaus despite substantial remaining evaluation budgets. We investigate \emph{principle-level search collapse}, where an optimizer's search becomes confined to a narrow set of design principles, even though it may continue to generate distinct candidates and achieve small improvements. We assemble a diagnostic benchmark spanning molecular optimization, network sentinel-node selection, and GPU-kernel optimization, and introduce a decision-tree protocol combining principle narrowing, prolonged performance plateaus, and gaps to attainable reference solutions. Across 161 assessable runs on the three problem domains, 78.3\% receive support for collapse, including 55.3\% with strong support. Candidate-level variation can nevertheless conceal restricted search at the principle level. We then test \emph{diversity injection}, a common response to search stagnation, such as higher t, multiple LLMs, and web search, and show that it provides limited and inconsistent benefits: among 65 molecular runs, still 73.8\% and 53.8\% receive support and strong support respectively. We finally test reference-principle interventions and find that they improve some runs, but their benefits vary across models and tasks: access to a better principle does not guarantee its effective use. Our benchmark and diagnostic protocol provide a basis for evaluating future optimizers on principle-level collapse. Our findings highlight the need for online collapse detection and better mechanisms for generating and maintaining alternative principles during optimization.

papers.title: ACTS: Learning Visuo-Tactile World Models from Human Physical Interaction
papers.abstract: Abstract   Action-conditioned world models for contact-rich manipulation require data that captures how contact forms, slides, and releases under varying force. Such data are slow to collect through robot teleoperation, which often lacks force feedback and is constrained by gripper geometry. We ask whether these dynamics can instead be learned from human physical interaction and transferred to a robot.   We present ACTS, a visuo-tactile world model trained only on human interaction data. Operators manipulate handheld GelSight sensors while we record third-person and wrist video, tactile images, 6-DoF sensor motion, and tactile-derived normal force, yielding React, a 4.9-hour bimanual dataset across three objects. We represent actions at the tactile sensor as motion augmented by force change, providing a shared action space for human collection and robot execution. ACTS jointly predicts future scene, wrist, and tactile observations.   On held-out human data, ACTS improves scene-view prediction by 0.7-2.0 dB PSNR over the stronger of two visuo-tactile world models trained from scratch on React. Without fine-tuning, in the robot teleoperation rollouts we inspected, predicted tactile imprints still appear and disappear with recorded contact. Visual transfer is less robust: camera predictions exceed frame copying on PushT, are mixed on Rope, and fall below it on Motherboard, while wrist views can blur or hallucinate structure. These results suggest that contact dynamics transfer more reliably than visual appearance from human to robot.

papers.title: CoCoNet: Convex Conformal Network for Multi-Dimensional Uncertainty Regions
papers.abstract: Conformal prediction (CP) provides distribution-free coverage guarantees under exchangeability, but the efficiency of its prediction regions depends critically on the choice of the conformity score. This is particularly important in multivariate regression, where dependencies across output dimensions induce complex joint uncertainty structures. This paper introduces CoCoNet (Convex Conformal Network) for learning convex conformity scores that induce flexible, data-adaptive prediction regions. CoCoNet learns the score from held-out data by optimizing prediction-region efficiency while enforcing convexity with respect to the residual. CoCoNet then applies split-conformal calibration to retain finite-sample coverage guarantees. The paper presents two variants of the method: CoCoNet$_{\mathrm{Spline}}$, based on piecewise-linear scores, and CoCoNet$_{\mathrm{ICNN}}$, based on Input Convex Neural Networks. Experiments compare CoCoNet with other CP baselines over synthetic and real-world datasets with output dimensions ranging from 2 to 16. The results demonstrate the flexibility of CoCoNet in learning different response types. Across 8 models and 30 multi-dimensional regression tasks, CoCoNet$_\text{ICNN}$ and CoCoNet$_{\mathrm{Spline}\text{-}\ell_1}$ achieve the best efficiencies with average ranks of 1.45 and 2.75, respectively. In particular, CoCoNet$_\text{ICNN}$ ranks first on 22 tasks out of 30 in terms of efficiency.

papers.title: Towards Reinforcement Learning for Space Robotics: Fast Training and Reliable Real-World Transfer
papers.abstract: This work demonstrates the use of a fast simulation-based training framework to learn control policies using reinforcement learning. The hardware requirements are minimal and the simulation-learned policies transfer reliably to the real world. With this setup, we show that a quadruped robot can learn to traverse diverse real-world terrains reliably---including in a lunar-analog facility---after less than 20 minutes of training on a single consumer-grade GPU. These results provide a glimpse of a future where reinforcement learning is a crucial tool in developing more capable and robust space robotic systems. papers.title: Data-Driven Resource Aggregation for Scalable Digital Twin and Simulation Model Generation
papers.abstract: As industrial digitization accelerates, the use of digital twins has become widespread. However, modern manufacturing systems are highly dynamic and frequently reconfigured, making manual model development and updates increasingly difficult. Recent research on automated simulation model generation shows that historical data such as event logs can yield simulation models automatically. However, modeling every resource at full granularity leads to unnecessary complexity and computational cost. We propose a method for automatically selecting and aggregating resources to simplify simulation modeling. Our method uses ideas from inverse reinforcement learning to learn behavioral value representations of resources from production event logs. This process identifies and aggregates resources with similar functional contributions. Experiments on manufacturing systems, using throughput and system time as performance measures, demonstrate that value-based resource aggregation performs well when the goal is to substantially reduce complexity while preserving performance accuracy.

papers.title: Switch-Time-Aware Hybrid Model Predictive Control Using the Hybrid Minimum Principle
papers.abstract: This article presents a time-aware hybrid model predictive control (MPC) framework that simultaneously optimizes the objective with respect to both continuous control inputs and event switching times. Rather than relying on a fixed time grid, the switching instant is lifted into the decision vector and treated as an explicit optimization variable. The resulting transcription is a smooth nonlinear program whose Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) conditions are consistent with the Hybrid Minimum Principle (HMP) event-time stationarity condition, so first-order hybrid sensitivities are recovered implicitly through the KKT system rather than by evaluating saltation matrices. Each MPC step solves a single sparse Quadratic Program (QP), jointly optimizing control inputs and impact timing in real time. On a bouncing mass landing on an oscillating platform, the method attaches in half the time of fixed-grid saltation MPC, reduces cumulative control effort by 30%, and removes the post-impact rebounds, at a 15% increase in per-cycle solve time. It matches the cumulative effort of offline time-aware solvers to within 4% while running at 2.4 ms per cycle against 281 ms for a complementarity-based formulation of the same problem, of which a 10.6x reduction is attributable to the transcription alone at a fixed solver.

papers.title: Neural Adjoint Inverse Design of Three‐Dimensional Nanophotonic Devices
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Volumetric meta‐optics have emerged as a compact high‐performance platform for advanced imaging, color routing in image sensors, and on‐chip wavefront control. Realizing such devices depends on solving a high‐dimensional nonconvex inverse‐design problem governed by Maxwell's equations. Adjoint optimization is the standard route to gradients, yet broadband three‐dimensional (3D) design typically requires thousands of full‐wave forward/adjoint simulations, making industrial‐scale optimization prohibitively slow. To address this bottleneck, a neural adjoint method is introduced, in which a solver‐supervised Fourier neural operator (FNO) directly predicts dense, per‐voxel 3D adjoint gradient fields from a voxelized permittivity volume. To preserve the sharp, resonance‐driven sensitivity peaks that single‐pass operator networks tend to oversmooth, a stage‐wise FNO is proposed, in which successive stages refine residual errors with progressively higher‐frequency emphasis. A domain‐specific dataset is curated from paired forward/adjoint finite‐difference time‐domain (FDTD) simulations spanning three volumetric tasks: spectral sorting (color routers), achromatic focusing (metalenses), and waveguide mode conversion. Across all benchmarks, the surrogate‐driven optimization attains figures of merit within 86%–99% of rigorous FDTD‐based adjoint optimization whilst reducing end‐to‐end design time from hours to seconds, with speedups exceeding . These results establish a pathway toward fast large‐scale volumetric meta‐optical design enabled by neural‐operator surrogates.

papers.title: Opportunities and Challenges in the Evidence-Informed Design of an Educational Escape Game for Veterinary Public Health Education Using Food-Borne Outbreak Investigation Data
papers.abstract: Abstract Food-borne outbreak management is a core competency in veterinary public health curricula. We developed an immersive, team-based educational escape game informed by evidence from documented food-borne outbreaks, designed to train veterinary students in health alert management. The scenario simulates a food-borne outbreak after a corporate cocktail reception and leads participants through successive parts of investigation: analytical epidemiology, selection and interpretation of microbiological tests, official-style inspection of a catering facility, and formulation of corrective and preventive measures. The targeted pathogen selected was Campylobacter spp. because of its major public health importance and relative underrepresentation in early veterinary curricula. The epidemiological data set was parameterized to support a staged learning progression using two successive case series and a rapid case–control framework. Symptom distributions, incubation periods, and plausible noise sources were incorporated to reflect common limitations of real outbreak investigations and to encourage critical interpretation of evidence. Visual inspection materials and forward-flow principles were developed to strengthen realism. The resulting game provides a coherent learning environment where students must integrate multiple sources of evidence, work collaboratively under time constraints, and justify decisions in conditions that approximate real outbreak investigations. By translating scientific and surveillance data into an interactive pedagogical format, the approach promotes active learning while maintaining epidemiological plausibility and professional relevance. This article details the rationale underpinning these design choices, discusses educational implications within a veterinary public health–compatible perspective, and highlights limitations and trade-offs required to translate complex outbreak situations into a time-limited learning activity.

papers.abstract: This research was motivated by the low concentration level of children aged 5–6 years at RA Bahrul 'Ilmi Dharmasraya due to conventional and repetitive learning methods. This study aims to describe and analyze the effectiveness of implementing the High Scope learning model in improving children's concentration during learning activities. Using a descriptive qualitative approach, this study involved 13 children from Group B and a classroom teacher as primary data sources. Data were collected through participatory observation, semi-structured interviews, and documentation across seven sessions, then analyzed descriptively. The results showed that the High Scope learning model was implemented effectively through active learning, the plan-do-review cycle, teacher scaffolding, and center-based environmental arrangements. Following the intervention, 11 out of 13 children (84.62%) experienced a significant increase in concentration, with 15% reaching Very Well Developed (BSB) and 62% reaching As Expected (BSH). Concentration duration increased from <10 minutes to 8–25 minutes, accompanied by reduced distraction levels, improved task completion, and enhanced recall abilities. Thus, the High Scope model is effective in enhancing early childhood learning concentration.

papers.title: Teaching Computer Science in the Digital and AI Era: Current Methods, Pedagogical Challenges, and Future Directions
papers.abstract: This article critically reviews the current state of computer science and informatics teaching and develops a practical framework for its improvement in the digital and artificial-intelligence era. The study adopts a structured narrative-review approach and synthesizes international standards, systematic reviews, and recent scholarship on programming education, computational thinking, active learning, mobile learning, digital competence, data literacy, Internet of Things (IoT), and artificial intelligence in education. The analysis shows that effective computer science teaching is not defined by the presence of technology alone. Learning outcomes depend on the alignment of pedagogy, content, learner readiness, teacher competence, assessment, and technological infrastructure. Direct explanation and demonstration remain valuable for introducing unfamiliar concepts, but they are most effective when followed by purposeful practice, debugging, problem solving, collaborative work, projects, and reflective feedback. Recent evidence supports flipped learning, gamification, mobile tools, and other active methodologies when they are connected to clearly specified learning objectives rather than used as isolated innovations. The review also argues that contemporary curricula should extend beyond software operation toward computational thinking, data reasoning, AI literacy, digital ethics, cybersecurity, and the ability to design and evaluate technological solutions. Based on the synthesis, the article proposes a balanced instructional model that combines explicit teaching, guided practice, inquiry, collaborative construction, authentic projects, and formative assessment. It concludes that the future of computer science education depends on pedagogically justified technology integration, continuous teacher development, inclusive access, and the responsible use of AI.

papers.title: The future of 3D bioprinting: From functional tissues to standardized manufacturing and clinical translation
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) bioprinting has evolved from demonstrating the feasibility of fabricating complex tissue architectures to engineering increasingly functional biological constructs. However, advances in biological functionality have not been matched by comparable progress in standardized evaluation, manufacturing consistency, and clinical translation. Here, we propose a Bioprinting 1.0 to 5.0 evolutionary framework that describes the progression of the field from engineering feasibility and biological compatibility to biological functionality, standardized manufacturing, and clinical translation. We discuss emerging standardization efforts across extrusion-, jetting-, and vat photopolymerization–based bioprinting and highlight the need for quantitative, reproducible benchmarks spanning bio-ink properties, printing performance, construct quality, and biological function. We further examine the manufacturing, safety, regulatory, and clinical requirements needed to translate functional bioprinted tissues into therapeutic products. This framework provides a roadmap for advancing 3D bioprinting from laboratory-scale demonstrations toward reproducible and clinically translatable tissue engineering.

papers.title: Possibilities and limitations of the adoption of active methodologies in school physical education
papers.abstract: School Physical Education, as a compulsory curricular component, plays an essential role in student development by integrating physical, cognitive, affective, and social aspects. Given the ongoing changes in education, there is a clear need to rethink teaching practices through active methodologies, which place students at the center of the learning process through action, reflection, and collaboration. This theoretical essay and literature review aims to analyze the impacts and practical possibilities of active learning in Physical Education classes. The study was based on 24 theoretical and scientific sources, including foundational books, peer-reviewed journal articles, a master's thesis, and official educational documents, particularly the Brazilian National Education Guidelines Law (LDB nº 9.394/1996). The analysis indicates that learning becomes truly meaningful when students actively engage in the process, connecting movement culture with their prior knowledge and personal experiences. Strategies such as TBL, PjBL, PBL, Constructivist Spiral, Flipped Classroom, and Maguerez's Arch enrich the teacher's pedagogical toolkit beyond repetitive drills. Ultimately, active methodologies represent valuable teaching alternatives, but they do not serve as an isolated magic solution for all educational challenges, requiring deliberate planning and ongoing teacher development

papers.title: Effect of re-melting on residual stresses in Inconel 718 produced by additive manufacturing
papers.abstract: Laser powder bed fusion (PBF-LB) fabricated Inconel 718 undergoes harsh thermal cycles that lead to the accumulation of residual stresses, which in turn degrades geometric accuracy and results in the deterioration of mechanical properties. To alleviate these residual stresses, the re-melting strategy has been proposed. In this study, the influence of different re-melting energy densities, E V , on the microstructures and residual stresses of Inconel 718 was investigated. The residual stresses in the builds were assessed using an innovative specimen cutting method. While increasing the E V to up to 0.4 times the first-pass energy increases the RS, at energies ≥ 0.9–1.3 times the first-pass energy led to a more uniform texture, lower RS and minimal porosity. Further increase in the E V led to an increase in porosity and RS. Other mechanical properties, such as yield strength and ductility are insensitive to E V . These results are explained on the basis of changes in the melt pool geometry and thermal gradients with increasing E V . This study highlights the potential of using re-melting to alleviate residual stresses with minimal post-processing treatments.

papers.title: Uncertainty-informed alloy design for additive manufacturing via a multi-functional large language model
papers.abstract: Integrating uncertainty quantification efficiently in alloy design is critical to achieve reliable properties in additively manufactured components for critical applications. Recent progress in applying large language models to conduct physics-based alloy design (e.g., AlloyGPT) has demonstrated a unique potential in handling multiple tasks of a forward prediction and inverse design of composition-structure–property relationships within a unified model. Here, the AlloyGPT model is extended and analyzed to enable uncertainty-informed robust alloy design. A dataset of 500,000 compositions spanning the standardized chemistry of model Alloy 718 was generated. Yield strengths for the fully heat-treated condition at room temperature were calculated using Calculation of Phase Diagrams (CALPHAD)-based simulations and analytical models. Local perturbation of composition by ±0.10 wt% variations led to 38–80 MPa changes in yield strength. The uncertainties were integrated in the text form to train the alloy-specific language model. AlloyGPT predicts mean yield strength and standard deviation with high accuracy. It also successfully performed constraint-driven inverse design of compositions satisfying a 1050 MPa target strength under standard-deviation constraints of 43–53 MPa and revealed a diverse set of feasible compositional solutions. To achieve both high-strength and resilience to additive manufacturing-induced compositional variation, the model-suggested compositional windows highlight the need for control of critical elements (i.e., Al, Ti, Cr), while allowing broader flexibility for Ni, Nb, Mo, and Co. The choice of critical elements was consistent with results from sensitivity analyses. These explorations and advancements are expected to establish an uncertainty-informed, multi-functional language model that targets a property and a bounded uncertainty simultaneously.

papers.title: Study of the mechanical properties of TiNi-based lattice structures produced by selective laser melting
papers.abstract: The properties of the initial TiNi powder and lattice specimens fabricated from it by selective laser melting (SLM), were investigated, and the factors affecting their mechanical performance were identified. The particle-size distribution and particle shape characteristics were determined by laser diffraction, while the elemental composition of the initial powder was determined by energy- dispersive X -ray fluorescence spectroscopy. X -ray computed tomography was performed on both the powder sample and the fabricated specimens. The processing characteristics of the powder were evaluated in accordance with the applicable GOST standards. Spiral and sinusoidal lattice specimens were fabricated by SLM. Their stress–strain response was simulated using the finite element method. The specimens were then subjected to compression testing followed by fractographic examination. The powder contained 45.41 wt. % Ti and 54.59 wt. % Ni, and no foreign particles were detected. Particle sizes ranged from 5 to 63 μm, with a median particle size of 33.566 μm. The bulk density, tapped density, and Hall flow rate were 3.92 g/cm 3 , 4.29 g/cm 3 , and 17.1 s/50 g, respectively. Sinusoidal and spiral specimens with a diameter of 2 mm, a height of 15 mm, and a strut thickness of 150 μm were produced by SLM. The numerical results showed that the maximum von Mises equivalent stresses in the struts reached the yield strength of the material and was concentrated at the junctions where the struts began to branch. Compression testing yielded stress-strain curves for the specimens in different cross-sections. The stresses in the central regions of the strut junctions were 173.25 ± 8.67 MPa for the sinusoidal structures and 148.75 ± 7.44 MPa for the spiral structures, whereas the stresses in the strut branching regions were 74.93 ± 7.50 MPa and 74.38 ± 7.44 MPa, respectively. Fractographic analysis revealed a mixed fracture mechanism.

papers.title: Development and characterization of mechanical metamaterials with a nature-inspired geometry
papers.abstract: One promising and innovative approaches to designing mechanical metamaterials for a range of applications is to draw on geometries found in natural structures. Nature offers a wide variety of geometries and structures that have evolved over long periods to serve different functions, including protection. Two such protective structures are the microstructure of pomelo peel and the geometry of carambola fruit, both of which help cushion the fruit against impact when it falls from a height. These structures can serve as prototypes for lightweight, high- strength metamaterials with enhanced energy absorption performance. Additive manufacturing enables the fabrication of such metamaterials with unit-cell geometries of arbitrary complexity. In this study, the microstructure of pomelo peel was used as the reference geometry for metamaterial design. Metamaterial samples comprising 5×5×5 unit cells with a nominal porosity of 80 % were fabricated from VT6 (Ti–6Al–4V) alloy by selective laser melting. Quasi-static and dynamic compression tests were performed to determine the mechanical properties and specific energy absorption of the metamaterials. The ultimate compressive strength of the metamaterial samples was 116 MPa, the yield strength was 102 MPa, and the effective elastic modulus was 6 GPa. Their specific energy absorption was 2.57 J/g under quasi-static compression and 2.71 J/g under dynamic compression. These findings demonstrate the potential nature-inspired design principle for developing energy-absorbing metamaterials and provide a basis for further research and the development of energy-absorbing systems and components.

papers.title: Spatiotemporal Prediction of Lake Water Quality Using Kriging, Geographically Weighted Regression, and Spatial Gating
papers.abstract: Accelerating eutrophication and dissolved oxygen depletion threaten freshwater ecosystems globally, yet predictive modeling remains difficult under sparse, irregularly sampled monitoring conditions.This study evaluates whether spatially engineered features from Ordinary Kriging and Geographically Weighted Regression improve dualtarget prediction of chlorophyll-a and dissolved oxygen across nine trophically diverse lakes using the LakeBeD-US benchmark, which exhibits missing-value rates above 85% and gaps up to 456 days.A spatiotemporal framework integrating both spatial methods with temporally aware architectures is proposed, alongside a Spatial Gating Module evaluated through a dedicated four-variant ablation study and two contemporary general-purpose architectural comparators, a Kolmogorov-Arnold Network and a Physics-Informed Neural Network Hybrid, under 144 controlled experimental configurations with a strict chronological, leakage-safe split.Under a rank-based aggregation criterion, Temporal + Kriging achieved the lowest mean RMSE rank for chlorophyll-a while Temporal + GWR did so for dissolved oxygen; however, pairwise Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with Bonferroni and Benjamini-Hochberg corrections confirmed that no integration scenario significantly outperformed the temporal-only baseline for either target, with statistically confirmed distinctions limited to the inferior performance of spatial-only configurations.Kriging-derived features are shown to act as trophic contextual priors rather than independent predictors, and practical monitoring claims are moderated accordingly.

papers.title: Capturing within-city heterogeneity in urban building energy models: A systematic review of microclimate, morphology, and occupancy
papers.abstract: Urban Building Energy Models (UBEMs) often smooth over differences within cities. This systematic review examines how urban and building morphology, local microclimate, and occupancy behavior contribute to within-city variation in building energy use. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, we reviewed 114 peer-reviewed studies using a structured narrative synthesis and descriptive evidence mapping, separating physical energy effects from methodological improvements. Reported physical effects were bidirectional, while thermostat settings and urban density frequently appeared among the highest-ranked sensitivity factors; the evidence does not support a universal hierarchy. Of 18 matched comparisons from eight studies, 17 reported lower model error and one was unchanged, although metrics, baselines, and validation designs differed. The literature supports context-specific representation of morphology, microclimate, and occupancy, together with empirical validation. Existing approaches range from one-way localized weather forcing and co-located inputs to two-way physical climate–building coupling. No reviewed implementation independently validated a complete dynamic loop linking morphology, microclimate, adaptive occupancy, building demand, and heat rejection. Further development requires sensor-supported data integration, multi-scale coupling, and uncertainty quantification.

papers.title: A task-oriented deep learning surrogate model for nonlinear seismic response prediction of deck-type RC arch bridge
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of seismic responses is essential for the safety assessment of long-span bridges. To address the challenges of coupled response behaviour and high computational cost in nonlinear time-history analysis of deck-type reinforced concrete (RC) arch bridges, a finite element (FE) model is developed to generate a seismic response dataset for data-driven modelling. A task-oriented Att-CNN-LSTM framework is proposed for seismic response prediction. The model employs gated causal convolution to extract local temporal features, followed by LSTM temporal modelling for capturing long-range dependencies and the attention mechanism for adaptive feature weighting across the sequence. Performance is evaluated using multiple metrics and statistical tests against LSTM, AttLSTM, CNN-LSTM, and WaveNet baselines. Results show that the proposed model achieves favourable prediction accuracy and efficiency, with coefficients of determination (R 2 ) ranging from 0.83 to 0.91 across different response quantities, while reducing the parameter count to approximately 16.6% of that of WaveNet. These results indicate that the proposed framework provides a viable and computationally efficient approach for capturing complex seismic response patterns in deck-type RC arch bridges, serving as a reliable surrogate model for rapid seismic assessment of deck-type RC arch bridges.

papers.title: Orientation and fiber content effects on the mechanical and microstructural properties of additively manufactured CFR-PEEK composites for cranio-maxillofacial implants
papers.abstract: Customized implants manufactured from carbon fiber-reinforced polyetheretherketone (CFR-PEEK) using fused filament fabrication (FFF) offer advantages over metallic implants, including radiolucency, reduced stress shielding, and design freedom. However, the combined effects of fiber content, build orientation, and processing-induced microstructure on mechanical performance remain insufficiently understood. In this study, unfilled PEEK, 12 vol% CFR-PEEK, and 20 vol% CFR-PEEK were fabricated in three build orientations (XY, XZ, Z) and characterized using tensile, flexural, and impact testing, complemented by scanning electron microscopy (SEM), micro-computed tomography (micro-CT), and differential scanning calorimetry (DSC). Results show that processing-induced defects strongly influence mechanical performance and can outweigh nominal reinforcement effects. Despite higher fiber content, 20 vol% CFR-PEEK exhibited lower Z-oriented tensile strength (56 MPa) than 12 vol% CFR-PEEK (75 MPa), attributable to a ninefold increase in void content (7.8% vs. 0.9%). In contrast, 20 vol% CFR-PEEK achieved the highest flexural modulus (14.1 GPa) and quasi-isotropic impact behavior. Micro-CT revealed fiber alignment parallel to the deposition direction and reduced void content during fabrication (38% for 12 vol% CFR-PEEK), while SEM confirmed improved fiber-matrix adhesion. These findings demonstrate that optimal fiber loading depends on both processing quality and loading mode, providing design-relevant guidance for FFF of CFR-PEEK components in biomedical implant applications.
